statement: The leading rational constant 2^(-8) may be discarded from the cuspidal Legendre Tate Kummer class, so exponent divisibility alone forces the asserted residual splitting.
Y1(7)(Q) is empty, so rational order-seven torsion can be excluded on that basis.

[Finite descent and every derived quotient] \label{thm:transfer} Suppose $g(X)\geq1$, $\#D(\bar k)\geq2$, and $X(\A_k)_\bullet^{\mathrm{f\text{-}ab}}=X(k)$. For every $m\geq1$ and for the maximal geometrically prosolvable quotient, \begin{equation} \Sec^{\pc}_{\Sel}(U/k)= U(k)\ \sqcup\ \coprod_{Q\in D(k)}H^1(k,\wh\Z(1)), \label{eq:classification} \end{equation} where the maps on the right are the ordinary point maps and the cusp packet maps, respectively. In particular, if $X(k)\subset D(k)$ every such Selmer section is cuspidal.

statement: All finite-derived and prosolvable Selmer sections are cuspidal for odd n divisible by 3,5 or7.
\label{prop:isogeny} There is a rational isogeny $\Jac(X_5)\sim A^3$.

statement: \label{prop:arithmetic} The groups $A(\Q)$ and $\Sha(\Q,A)$ are finite. More precisely $A(\Q)\cong\Z/5\Z$ and \begin{equation} C(\Q)=\{\infty,(0,0),(0,-1)\}. \label{eq:cpoints} \end{equation} Consequently $\Jac(X_5)(\Q)$ and $\Sha(\Q,\Jac(X_5))$ are finite.

statement: [Explicit restricted pro-$3$ cases] \label{thm:restrictedintro} Let $n=3^r$, $r\geq1$, and let $N=\pi_1((U_n)_{\bar\Q})^{(3)}$. Fix a rational coordinate tangent with leading coefficient one, extending over $\Z[1/3]$. Let $M=N/J$ where $J$ is closed, normal, Galois stable, and contained in $[N,N]$; in particular $M=N$ is allowed. Take any of \[ S=\{3\},\qquad S=\{3,7\},\qquad S=\{3,q\}\quad(q\text{ prime},\ q\equiv2\text{ or }5\pmod9). \] Every section of $M\rtimes G_\Q$ whose entire relative cocycle is trivial on inertia outside $S$, and whose restriction at $3$ is point-or-cusp geometric, is globally cuspidal. Such sections form three disjoint cusp packets, each parametrized by $\bigoplus_{q\in S}\Z_3\kappa_3(q)$. They satisfy the point-or-cusp condition at every place.
depends_on: Shafarevich1963 p82; actual tangential action; exact local Kummer/source calculations; independent cubic isogeny descent; equivariant freeness; pullback/norm and boundary cocycles

statement: Continuum many noncuspidal full geometric pro-3 sections of U3/Q exist with whole cocycles unramified outside3; all fail local geometry at3.
[Exponent one]\label{prop:one} For $n=1$, the all-cuspidal Selmer assertion is false for every geometric quotient considered in this paper, including the full geometrically pro-$3$ group.

statement: [Odd Fermat exponents with known descent targets] \label{thm:quintic} Let $n\geq3$ be odd and divisible by at least one of $3$, $5$, $7$, or $11$, and put \[ X_n:\ X^n+Y^n+Z^n=0,\qquad U_n=X_n\setminus\{XYZ=0\}. \] For every finite derived quotient, including the geometrically metabelian quotient, and for the maximal geometrically prosolvable quotient, every point-or-cusp Selmer section is cuspidal. There are exactly three cusp centers, $[0:1:-1]$, $[1:0:-1]$, and $[1:-1:0]$, each with its full completed Kummer packet $H^1(\Q,\wh\Z(1))$.
depends_on: thm:transfer; prop:arithmetic; prop:eleven; StollCorollary8.8; Elkies1998 pp68-74; Kriz-Li2019 section10.1

statement: [Arbitrary pro-$3$ sections and the local obstruction] \label{thm:arbitraryintro} For every $n=3^r$, $r\geq1$, there are continuum many pairwise geometrically nonconjugate sections of the full geometrically pro-$3$ arithmetic fundamental group of $U_n/\Q$ whose entire cocycles relative to a standard integral tangent are unramified outside $3$ and whose compact classes in $H^1(\Q,T_3E)$, for $E:v^2+v=u^3-7$, have infinite order. They are noncuspidal, and each restriction at $3$ is neither point geometric nor cusp geometric. In particular none is a point-or-cusp Selmer section. Their noncuspidality, pairwise nonconjugacy, and local obstruction persist in every Galois-stable geometric quotient retaining the geometric abelianization. A second family of continuum many sections has zero class in $H^1(\Q,T_3\Jac(X_n))$, with the same ramification, nonconjugacy, and local obstruction; its two boundary valuation coordinates can be chosen as $(1,b)$ for $b\in3+9\Z_3$.
depends_on: Shafarevich1963 p82; actual tangential action; exact local Kummer/source calculations; independent cubic isogeny descent; equivariant freeness; pullback/norm and boundary cocycles

statement: The pro3 abelian Selmer sections of U3 are precisely three rational cusp packets H1(Q,Z3(1)); their whole local geometric inertia is determined by the cusp parameter.
For every n=3^r all full geometric pro3 Selmer sections are cuspidal, with exactly three H1(Q,Z3(1)) packets and no finite ramification restriction.
For U3 the same three-packet classification holds in every ordinary lower-central quotient N/gamma_cN, c>=2, without requiring a full global lift.

\label{prop:eleven} The groups $A_{11}(\Q)$ and $\Sha(\Q,A_{11})$ are finite, $A_{11}(\Q)\simeq\Z/11\Z$, and \[ C_{11}(\Q)=\{\infty,(0,0),(0,-1)\}. \] The central value satisfies \begin{equation} 1.78<L(A_{11}/\Q,1)<1.80. \label{eq:elevenvalue} \end{equation}

statement: \label{prop:boundaryfamily} For every $n=3^r$, $r\geq1$, there are continuum many pairwise geometrically nonconjugate full pro-$3$ sections of $U_n/\Q$ whose whole cocycles are unramified outside $3$ and whose classes in $H^1(\Q,T_3\Jac(X_n))$ are zero. Each fails point-or-cusp geometry at $3$. All these assertions persist after passing to any Galois-stable geometric quotient retaining $N_n^{\ab}$.

statement: \label{prop:rationalpositive} There is an exact rational certificate that $L(A/\Q,1)>1/20$.

statement: \label{prop:septic} The group $A_7(\mathbb Q)$ has order seven, and $\Sha(\mathbb Q,A_7)$ is finite. In particular the $3$-adic Selmer group of $T_3A_7$ is zero.

statement: [Local cuspidality at three] \label{thm:localthreeintro} Let $n\ge3$ be odd and divisible by at least one of $3$, $5$, $7$, or $11$. Put $N=\pi_1((U_n)_{\bar\Q})^{(3)}$, and let $M=N/J$, where $J$ is closed, normal, Galois stable, and contained in $[N,N]$. For every point-or-cusp Selmer section of the arithmetic quotient with geometric group $M$, its localization at $3$ is cuspidal at a rational coordinate cusp. This includes the geometric abelian quotient and the full geometric pro-$3$ group. Every full local geometric representative at $3$ has a cusp as its center. This local theorem alone does not prove global conjugacy to a cusp section; the global results for the three families above require their additional arithmetic arguments.
depends_on: Proper Selmer vanishing for m3,5,7,11; elementary four-point local Kummer locus and two proper quotient maps

statement: [Four points in the zero Kummer locus]\label{lem:fourzero} The points $Q\in C_m(\mathbb Q_3)$ whose classes $[Q-\infty]$ vanish in $A_m(\mathbb Q_3)^{\wedge3}$ are exactly \[ \infty,\quad (0,0),\quad(0,-1),\quad W_m=(a_m,-1/2),\qquad a_m^m=-1/4. \] Here $a_m$ is the unique such element of $\mathbb Q_3$.
depends_on: Proper Selmer vanishing for m3,5,7,11; elementary four-point local Kummer locus and two proper quotient maps

statement: [A vanishing proper Selmer group forces a local cusp]\label{prop:localtwomaps} Suppose the $3$-adic Selmer group of $T_3A_m$ is zero; equivalently, $A_m(\mathbb Q)^{\wedge3}=0$ and $T_3\Sha(\mathbb Q,A_m)=0$. For every odd multiple $n$ of $m$, the localization at $3$ of any point-or-cusp Selmer section of the geometrically pro-$3$ abelian quotient of $U_n/\mathbb Q$ is cuspidal at a rational coordinate cusp. The same conclusion holds for any geometric pro-$3$ quotient retaining that abelianization, including the full pro-$3$ group.
depends_on: Proper Selmer vanishing for m3,5,7,11; elementary four-point local Kummer locus and two proper quotient maps

statement: A finite rational Mordell-Weil target of dimension>=2 with surjective Jacobian map controls finite abelian descent if Tate-Sha vanishes for almost all rational primes completely split in one finite Galois extension.

\label{prop:thirteenpartial} The Fermat curve $X_{13}$ has a nonconstant rational morphism to an abelian fourfold $P_{13}$ such that \[ P_{13}(\Q)\simeq\Z/13\Z,\qquad 2.632<L(P_{13}/\Q,1)<2.636. \] Its conductor is $13^8$, its archimedean factor is $(2\pi)^{-4s}\Gamma(s)^4$, and its functional-equation sign is $+1$.

statement: [Local point/cusp separation] \label{prop:lm-local-metabelian-separation} Let $U_1=\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$ over $\mathbb Q_3$. No ordinary point section of $U_1(\mathbb Q_3)$ is cuspidal in the geometrically pro-$3$ metabelian quotient. The three rational cusp packets in that quotient are pairwise disjoint.

statement: [A nonzero relative localization kernel] \label{prop:mixed-kernel} If $m>1$ in Proposition~\ref{prop:mixed-transfer}, then \[ \ker\bigl(H^1(\Q,M)\longrightarrow H^1(\Q_3,M)\bigr)\ne0. \] This is a cohomological assertion. The constructed class is not asserted to be Selmer or to lift to a nonabelian section.

statement: For U3 every point-or-cusp Selmer section of each geometric finite-derived pro3 quotient is cuspidal, without assuming a global lift to the full quotient.

[Unrestricted pro-$3$ Selmer sections] \label{thm:unrestrictedintro} Let $n=3^r$, $r\ge1$, and put $N_n=\pi_1(U_{n,\overline\Q})^{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}3}$. Let $R$ be a $G_\Q$-stable quotient of $N_n$ such that $N_n^{\mathrm{ab}}\to R^{\mathrm{ab}}$ is an isomorphism and every closed ordinary lower-central factor $\gamma_mR/\gamma_{m+1}R$ is torsion-free over $\Z_3$. The point-or-cusp Selmer sections in the corresponding arithmetic quotient are exactly the three disjoint rational cusp packets, each parametrized by $H^1(\Q,\Z_3(1))$. In particular this holds for the full group $N_n$, every quotient $N_n/\gamma_cN_n$ with $c\ge2$, and every finite-derived quotient $N_n/N_n^{[d]}$ with $d\ge1$, including the maximal geometrically metabelian pro-$3$ quotient. Here $N_n^{[d]}$ is the closed derived series. No finite ramification hypothesis or global lift to the full group is assumed.

statement: [The affine abelianization separates the rational cusps] \label{prop:lm-affine-ab-cusp-separation} For every odd $n\ge3$, the three rational cusp packets of $U_n/\mathbb Q_3$ have pairwise disjoint images in the geometrically pro-$3$ abelian quotient. Consequently the three global rational cusp packets are also pairwise disjoint in that quotient. If $3\nmid n$, this assertion uses the affine abelianization: the compact Jacobian Kummer classes of the rational cusps are all equal.

statement: [A completely split-prime descent criterion] \label{thm:split-prime-descent} Let $X/\Q$ be a smooth proper geometrically connected curve with a nonconstant morphism $f:X\to A$ to an abelian variety. Suppose $A(\Q)$ is finite and $f(X)_{\bar\Q}$ is not a torsion translate of an elliptic subvariety. If a finite Galois extension $L/\Q$ satisfies \[ T_\ell\Sha(\Q,A)=0 \quad\text{for all but finitely many primes $\ell$ splitting completely in $L$}, \] then $X(\A_\Q)_\bullet^{\mathrm{f\text{-}ab}}=X(\Q)$. Thus Theorem~\ref{thm:transfer} applies to every affine open with at least two geometric boundary points. No rank or Tate--Shafarevich hypothesis over $L$ is required.
depends_on: Stoll2007 Proposition5.16 and Theorem8.2; Stoll2017 erratum; Pila-Zannier2008 Theorem1.1star

statement: [A conditional mixed-exponent criterion] \label{thm:mixedcompactintro} Let $n=3^r q^s$, where $r,s\ge1$ and $q$ is an odd prime with $q\equiv2$ or $5\pmod9$, and put $S=\{3,q\}$ and $J_n=\Jac(X_n)$. Write $\Sel(T_3J_n)$ for the integral $3$-adic Selmer group, whose local conditions are the Kummer images of $J_n(\Q_v)^{\wedge_3}$ at every finite place. Assume \[ \ker\bigl(\Sel(T_3J_n)\longrightarrow H^1(\Q_3,T_3J_n)\bigr)=0.\tag{$\mathrm C_n$} \] Then the point-or-cusp Selmer sections of the geometrically pro-$3$ abelian quotient of $U_n/\Q$ are exactly the three disjoint rational cusp packets, each parametrized by $H^1(\Q,\Z_3(1))$. More generally, let $R$ be a $G_\Q$-stable quotient of the geometric pro-$3$ group retaining its abelianization, with finite free ordinary lower-central factors $L_m=\gamma_mR/\gamma_{m+1}R$. The same conclusion holds in $R$ if, for every $m\ge2$, \[ L_m^{G_{\Q_3}}=0,\qquad \ker\bigl(H^1(G_{\Q,S},L_m)\longrightarrow H^1(\Q_3,L_m)\bigr)=0. \tag{$\mathrm G_m$} \] These are conditional assertions: neither $(\mathrm C_n)$ for these mixed Jacobians nor the additional conditions $(\mathrm G_m)$ are established here. Rank $J_n(\Q)=0$ together with $T_3\Sha(J_n/\Q)=0$ is sufficient for $(\mathrm C_n)$.
depends_on: Coleman1986 p191 cusp order; Rousseau1969 theorem p11-01 (Baker-Brumer); integral S-unit norm and Shapiro; existing central induction

statement: [Unrestricted pro-$3$ Selmer sections] \label{thm:unrestrictedmixedintro} Let $n=3^r$ or $n=5\cdot3^r$, with $r\ge1$, and put $N_n=\pi_1(U_{n,\overline\Q})^{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}3}$. Let $R$ be a $G_\Q$-stable quotient of $N_n$ such that $N_n^{\mathrm{ab}}\to R^{\mathrm{ab}}$ is an isomorphism and every closed ordinary lower-central factor $\gamma_mR/\gamma_{m+1}R$ is torsion-free over $\Z_3$. The point-or-cusp Selmer sections in the corresponding arithmetic quotient are exactly the three disjoint rational cusp packets, each parametrized by $H^1(\Q,\Z_3(1))$. In particular this holds for the full group $N_n$, every quotient $N_n/\gamma_cN_n$ with $c\ge2$, and every finite-derived quotient $N_n/N_n^{[d]}$ with $d\ge1$, including the maximal geometrically metabelian pro-$3$ quotient. Here $N_n^{[d]}$ is the closed derived series. No finite ramification hypothesis or global lift to the full group is assumed. For both exponent families, writing $J_n=\Jac(X_n)$, the compact integral Selmer localization is injective: \[ \ker\bigl(\Sel(T_3J_n)\longrightarrow H^1(\Q_3,T_3J_n)\bigr)=0. \] Here the local conditions defining $\Sel(T_3J_n)$ are the completed Mordell--Weil Kummer images at all finite places. No rank or Tate--Shafarevich hypothesis for the higher $J_n$ is required.

statement: [A conditional mixed-exponent criterion] \label{thm:realconditionalmixedintro} Let $n=3^r q^s$, where $r,s\ge1$ and $q$ is an odd prime with $q\ne3$. Assume $r=1$ or $q\equiv2,4,5,7\pmod9$, and put $S=\{3,q\}$ and $J_n=\Jac(X_n)$. Write $\Sel(T_3J_n)$ for the integral $3$-adic Selmer group, whose local conditions are the Kummer images of $J_n(\Q_v)^{\wedge_3}$ at every finite place. Assume \[ \ker\bigl(\Sel(T_3J_n)\longrightarrow H^1(\Q_3,T_3J_n)\bigr)=0.\tag{$\mathrm C_n$} \] Then the point-or-cusp Selmer sections of the geometrically pro-$3$ abelian quotient of $U_n/\Q$ are exactly the three disjoint rational cusp packets, each parametrized by $H^1(\Q,\Z_3(1))$. More generally, let $R$ be a $G_\Q$-stable quotient of the geometric pro-$3$ group retaining its abelianization, with finite free ordinary lower-central factors $L_m=\gamma_mR/\gamma_{m+1}R$. The same conclusion holds in $R$ if, for every $m\ge2$, \[ L_m^{G_{\Q_3}}=0,\qquad \ker\bigl(H^1(G_{\Q,S},L_m)\longrightarrow H^1(\Q_3,L_m)\bigr)=0. \tag{$\mathrm G_m$} \] The conditions $(\mathrm C_n)$ and $(\mathrm G_m)$ are proved here when $q=5$ or $7$ and $s=1$, giving the mixed families in Theorem~\ref{thm:unrestrictedthreefamiliesintro}. For the other exponents they remain explicit hypotheses. Rank $J_n(\Q)=0$ together with $T_3\Sha(J_n/\Q)=0$ is sufficient for $(\mathrm C_n)$. The exponent condition is exact for the boundary localization used here. For any odd prime $q\ne3$ and $r,s\ge1$, write the boundary Tate module as $B_n=\Z_3(1)[D_n(\bar\Q)]/\Z_3(1)\sum_{Q\in D_n}e_Q$. Choose distinct rational cusps $P,Q$, eliminate $e_Q$ using the diagonal relation, and split off $I_P=\Z_3(1)e_P$ to obtain $B_n=I_P\oplus M_n$. Then \[ H^1(G_{\Q,S},M_n)\longrightarrow H^1(\Q_3,M_n) \text{ is injective}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad r=1\ \text{or}\ q\equiv2,4,5,7\pmod9. \] Failure of this cohomological injectivity does not by itself produce a noncuspidal Selmer section.
depends_on: Coleman1986 p191; Brumer1968 p193 Remark1; integral Kummer and Shapiro; exact real q-prime criterion; central induction

statement: [A finite class-group criterion for the septic family] \label{thm:septicfiniteintro} Let $\alpha=\sqrt[7]{3}$ be real, let $z$ be either real root of \[ R(Z)=27Z^8-1323Z^6+6174Z^4-117649, \] and put $M=\Q(\alpha,z)$. This field has degree $56$, signature $(2,27)$, and discriminant $-3^{55}7^{62}$. Assume the finite class-group condition $\operatorname{Cl}(M)[3]=0$. Then, for every $n=7\cdot3^r$ with $r\ge1$, compact integral Selmer localization at three is injective, and every point-or-cusp Selmer section in a $G_\Q$-stable quotient of the geometric pro-$3$ group retaining abelianization and having torsion-free ordinary lower-central factors is globally cuspidal. The section set consists of precisely three disjoint rational cusp packets, each parametrized by $H^1(\Q,\Z_3(1))$. This includes the full group, every finite-derived quotient, and every finite ordinary lower-central quotient. The class-group condition is equivalent to $\operatorname{Cl}(K_7)[3]=0$ for $K_7=\Q(\Jac(v^2+v=u^7)[3])$, the degree-$336$ splitting field of $(T^7-3)R(T)$, whose absolute discriminant is $3^{330}7^{380}$. These field descriptions and the reduction to the finite condition are proved here; the class-group vanishing itself is not proved.

statement: [Unrestricted pro-$3$ Selmer sections] \label{thm:unrestrictedthreefamiliesintro} Let $n=3^r$, $n=5\cdot3^r$, or $n=7\cdot3^r$, with $r\ge1$, and put $N_n=\pi_1(U_{n,\overline\Q})^{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}3}$. For all three exponent families, writing $J_n=\Jac(X_n)$, the compact integral Selmer localization is injective: \[ \ker\bigl(\Sel(T_3J_n)\longrightarrow H^1(\Q_3,T_3J_n)\bigr)=0. \] Here the local conditions defining $\Sel(T_3J_n)$ are the completed Mordell--Weil Kummer images at all finite places. statement: [The exponent-thirteen split-prime arithmetic input] \label{thm:thirteen-selmer-intro} Let $\mathcal K:A^4B+B^4C+C^4A=0$, let $c[A:B:C]=[C:A:B]$, and put $B=\mathcal K/\langle c\rangle$. Define the rational abelian fourfold $P_{13}=(1-c)\Jac(\mathcal K)$, and put \[ K=\Q(\zeta_{13})^{\langle3\rangle},\qquad L=K\Q(\zeta_3). \] There is a nonconstant rational morphism $X_{13}\to P_{13}$ whose image generates $P_{13}$ by differences. Moreover, \[ P_{13}(\Q)\simeq\Z/13\Z,\qquad 2.632<L(P_{13}/\Q,1)<2.636. \] For all but finitely many rational primes $p$ splitting completely in the finite Galois extension $L/\Q$, \[ H^1_f(\Q,V_pP_{13})=0,\qquad T_p\Sha(P_{13}/\Q)=0, \qquad V_pP_{13}=T_pP_{13}\otimes_{\Z_p}\Q_p. \] Here $H^1_f$ is the rational Bloch--Kato Selmer group. Consequently $X_n(\A_\Q)_\bullet^{\mathrm{f\text{-}ab}}=X_n(\Q)$ for every positive multiple $n$ of $13$. No finiteness of the entire group $\Sha(P_{13}/\Q)$ is asserted.

There are exactly three cusp centers, $[0:1:-1]$, $[1:0:-1]$, and $[1:-1:0]$, each with its full completed Kummer packet $H^1(\Q,\wh\Z(1))$.

statement: [The exponent-nineteen arithmetic input] \label{thm:nineteen-selmer-intro} Let $C$ be the smooth projective curve $y^{19}=x(1-x)^7$, put $J=\Jac(C)$, and let \[ c(x,y)=\left(\frac1{1-x},-\frac{y^7}{(1-x)^3}\right), \qquad e=\frac{1+c+c^2}{3}. \] Let $A=\Jac(C/\langle c\rangle)$ and let $P$ be the image of $1-e$ in the rational isogeny category. Then \[ J\sim_\Q A\times P,\qquad \dim A=3,\quad\dim P=6, \qquad \operatorname{rank}A(\Q)=1,\quad \operatorname{rank}P(\Q)=0. \] The central derivative satisfies \[ 9.96<L'(J/\Q,1)<9.99. \] The groups $\Sha(J/\Q)$, $\Sha(A/\Q)$ and $\Sha(P/\Q)$ are finite. There is a nonconstant rational morphism $X_{19}\to P$ whose image generates $P$ by differences. Consequently $X_n(\A_\Q)_\bullet^{\mathrm{f\text{-}ab}}=X_n(\Q)$ for every positive multiple $n$ of $19$.

statement: [Compact Selmer localization] \label{thm:compact-small-primes-intro} Let $J_n=\Jac(X_n)$, and let $\Sel(T_3J_n)$ denote the integral Selmer group with completed Mordell--Weil Kummer images at every finite place. The localization map \[ \Sel(T_3J_n)\longrightarrow H^1(\Q_3,T_3J_n) \] is injective for \[ \begin{gathered} n=3^r\quad(r\ge1),\qquad n=5\cdot3^r\ \hbox{or}\ 7\cdot3^r\quad(r\ge0),\qquad n=11. \end{gathered} \] At $n=11$, the group $\Sha(J_{11}/\Q)$ is finite, $\operatorname{rank}J_{11}(\Q)=6$, and $\Sel(T_3J_{11})\simeq\Z_3^6$. More generally, for every rational prime $\ell$ the map \[ \Sel(T_\ell J_{11})\longrightarrow H^1(\Q_\ell,T_\ell J_{11}) \] is injective integrally, including at $\ell=11$. The base-exponent assertions at $5$, $7$, and $11$ concern compact localization; they do not enlarge the affine pro-$3$ classification in the next theorem.
depends_on: thm:eleven-compact-selmer; lem:rank-one-compact-localization; cor:compact-base-source-five-seven; thm:unrestrictedthreefamiliesintro

statement: [Local conclusions at exponent seventeen] \label{thm:seventeen-local-intro} The $17$-component of every point of $X_{17}(\A_\Q)_\bullet^{\mathrm{f\text{-}ab}}$ is one of the three rational coordinate cusps. The same holds for the compact local representative at $17$ of every point-or-cusp Selmer section of an all-prime finite-derived or prosolvable quotient of $\pi_1(U_{17})$. For every $n=17^r$, $r\ge1$, the integral compact localization \[ \Sel(\Q,T_{17}\Jac(X_n)) \longrightarrow H^1(\Q_{17},T_{17}\Jac(X_n)) \] is injective, with no rank or Tate--Shafarevich finiteness hypothesis. These statements determine one local component and one coefficient prime. They do not establish the all-prime global cusp classification at exponent seventeen.
depends_on: McCallum1994 Propositions2/3/5/7,Theorems3/4/5,Lemmas7-10 pp569-582; McCallum2001 Lemma1/equation5 authorpp4-5; Washington1982 Theorem5.34p78; Stoll2007 Corollary7.3p379 and Theorem8.2; pointed arithmetic source

statement: [A finite-descent criterion allowing positive rank] \label{thm:positive-rank-split-intro} Let $X/\Q$ be a smooth proper curve of genus at least one with $O\in X(\Q)$, let $f:X\to A$ be a morphism to an abelian variety, and let $Z\subset X$ be a finite $\Q$-subscheme. Suppose that a finite Galois extension $L/\Q$ has the following property: for all but finitely many rational primes $\ell$ splitting completely in $L$, one has $T_\ell\Sha(A/\Q)=0$ and \[ \left\{x\in X(\Q_\ell): \log_\ell(f(x)-f(O))\in \operatorname{span}_{\Q_\ell}\log_\ell A(\Q)\right\} \subset Z(\Q_\ell). \] Then $X(\A_\Q)_\bullet^{\mathrm{f\text{-}ab}}=X(\Q)\subset Z(\Q)$. The local logarithmic condition has not been proved for a sufficient set of split primes at exponent seventeen.
depends_on: Stoll2007 multiplication-torsor Selmer description, Proposition5.16 and Theorem8.2; Stoll2017 errata; local logarithm hypothesis

statement: [Regular-prime localization and local Brauer support] \label{thm:regular-local-intro} Let $p$ be an odd regular prime, meaning $p\nmid h(\Q(\zeta_p))$, and let $n=p^r$, $r\ge1$. For $J_n=\Jac(X_n)$, the maps \[ H^1(G_{\Q,\{p\}},T_pJ_n) \longrightarrow H^1(\Q_p,T_pJ_n),\qquad \Sel(\Q,T_pJ_n)\longrightarrow H^1(\Q_p,T_pJ_n) \] are injective integrally. Here $G_{\Q,\{p\}}$ denotes the quotient unramified at finite primes other than $p$. No rank or Tate--Shafarevich finiteness hypothesis is needed. At exponent seventeen, the $17$-component of every point of $X_{17}(\A_\Q)_\bullet^{\mathrm{f\text{-}ab}}$ is one of the three rational coordinate cusps. The same holds for the compact local representative at $17$ of every point-or-cusp Selmer section of an all-prime finite-derived or prosolvable quotient of $\pi_1(U_{17})$. These local assertions do not establish the all-prime global cusp classification at exponent seventeen.
depends_on: McCallum1994 Propositions2/3/5/7,Theorems3/4/5,Lemmas7-10 pp569-582; McCallum2001 Lemma1/equation5 authorpp4-5; Washington1982 Theorem5.34p78; Stoll2007 Corollary7.3p379 and Theorem8.2; pointed arithmetic source

statement: [A Frey-three criterion in the prosolvable quotient] \label{thm:prosolvable-frey-three-intro} Let $n\ge3$ be odd, and let $s$ be a point-or-cusp Selmer section of the geometrically prosolvable quotient of $\pi_1(U_n)$. Identify $X_n$ with $X^n+Y^n=Z^n$, and pull back the three-adic Tate module of $E_\lambda:y^2=x(x-1)(x-\lambda)$, $\lambda=(X/Z)^n$, along $s$. This defines $\rho_s:G_\Q\to\operatorname{GL}_2(\Z_3)$ with determinant $\chi_3$. If $\rho_s\bmod9$ has a stable cyclic subgroup of order nine, then $s$ is globally cuspidal. In particular reducibility of $\rho_s$ over $\Q_3$ implies cuspidality. Every noncuspidal such section therefore has irreducible $\rho_s$, and its chosen proper local representatives are interior and integral for a set of primes of Dirichlet density one. This does not assert integrality outside a finite set, and the stable-subgroup hypothesis is not deduced from the Selmer condition.
depends_on: Solvable-cover core lemma; Stoll2007 Proposition8.5 Corollary8.8 with2017errata; Wiles1995 Theorem0.5; Stix2015 Section4.3 local Tate calculation; independent disconnected-monodromy trace proof

statement: [Open Frey images in the prosolvable quotient] \label{thm:prosolvable-frey-open-intro} Let $n\ge5$ be odd, and let $s$ be a point-or-cusp Selmer section of the geometrically prosolvable quotient of $\pi_1(U_n)$. In the model $X^n+Y^n=Z^n$, the Legendre family $E_\lambda:y^2=x(x-1)(x-\lambda)$, $\lambda=(X/Z)^n$, gives representations $\rho_{s,\ell}:G_\Q\to\operatorname{GL}_2(\Z_\ell)$, $\ell=2,3$, with determinant $\chi_\ell$. If $\rho_{s,3}\bmod9$ has a stable cyclic subgroup of order nine, then $s$ is globally cuspidal. If $s$ is not globally cuspidal, both representations are absolutely irreducible and have open images, and their joint image is open in $\operatorname{GL}_2(\Z_2)\times\operatorname{GL}_2(\Z_3)$. At a set of rational primes $q$ of Dirichlet density one, its local representatives are interior and integral and both representations have the same Frobenius polynomial $T^2-a_qT+q$, with $a_q\in\Z$ and complex roots of absolute value $q^{1/2}$. No common finite ramification set, modularity, or classification of this simultaneous open-image case is asserted. The exponent-three case is already classified by Theorem~\ref{thm:regular-solvable-intro}.
depends_on: Existing Frey3 criterion/density; Serre1989 II2.5 II3.4 III1.2 III2.2-2.3 proof; BrinonConrad2009 Lemma8.3.9; finite-level trace comparison and Goursat

statement: [Compact localization and full compact section images] \label{thm:compact-localization-sections-intro} Let $J_n=\Jac(X_n)$, and let $\Sel(T_3J_n)$ denote the integral Selmer group with completed Mordell--Weil Kummer images at every finite place. The localization map \[ \Sel(T_3J_n)\longrightarrow H^1(\Q_3,T_3J_n) \] is injective for \[ \begin{gathered} n=3^r\quad(r\ge1),\qquad n=5\cdot3^r\ \hbox{or}\ 7\cdot3^r\quad(r\ge0),\qquad n=11. \end{gathered} \] At $n=11$, the group $\Sha(J_{11}/\Q)$ is finite, $\operatorname{rank}J_{11}(\Q)=6$, and $\Sel(T_3J_{11})\simeq\Z_3^6$. More generally, for every rational prime $\ell$ the map \[ \Sel(T_\ell J_{11})\longrightarrow H^1(\Q_\ell,T_\ell J_{11}) \] is injective integrally, including at $\ell=11$. For $a=5,7$, let $N_a=\pi_1(U_{a,\overline\Q})^{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}3}$, let $I_a$ be the closed normal subgroup generated by its boundary inertia, and let $R$ be a stable quotient of $N_a$ retaining its abelianization. The compact quotient is $R^{\mathrm{cp}}=N_a/(\ker(N_a\to R)I_a)$. Every point-or-cusp Selmer section in $R$ has compact image globally conjugate to the image of the proper point section at a rational coordinate cusp supplied by its localization at $3$. This includes the full compact pro-$3$ image when $R=N_a$. These conclusions concern compact localization and compact section images; they do not enlarge the affine pro-$3$ classification in the next theorem.
depends_on: Existing pure/mixed sources; eleven arithmetic; prop:nonabelian-source-localization; cor:compact-full-base-five-seven

statement: [Regular-prime nonabelian localization] \label{thm:regular-nonabelian-localization-intro} Let $p$ be an odd regular prime, meaning $p\nmid h(\Q(\zeta_p))$, let $n=p^r$ with $r\ge1$, and use a standard integral rational cusp tangent on $U_n$. Write $N_n^{(p)}$ and $C_n^{(p)}$ for the full geometric pro-$p$ fundamental groups of $U_n$ and $X_n$. For $M=N_n^{(p)}$, $C_n^{(p)}$, or any finitely generated $G_\Q$-stable quotient, the entire map of pointed sets \[ H^1(G_{\Q,\{p\}},M)\longrightarrow H^1(\Q_p,M) \] is injective. Proper point-local Selmer sections of $C_n^{(p)}$ and its stable quotients are determined by their localization at $p$. The integral maps \[ H^1(G_{\Q,\{p\}},T_pJ_n)\longrightarrow H^1(\Q_p,T_pJ_n), \qquad \Sel(\Q,T_pJ_n)\longrightarrow H^1(\Q_p,T_pJ_n) \] are injective, with no rank or Tate--Shafarevich finiteness hypothesis.
depends_on: Proper cyclotomic Kummer torsors; McCallum1994 Sections3-5; Milne2006ADT I.3 and I.4.10(b); Washington1982; SGA1; Wojtkowiak2009; integral free-Lie and free-solvable inputs

statement: [Geometric pro-seventeen cusp classification] \label{thm:proseventeen-intro} Let $n=17^r$, $r\ge1$, and let $R$ be a $G_\Q$-stable quotient of $N_n^{(17)}$ inducing an isomorphism on abelianization. Suppose that every ordinary lower-central factor of $R$ is a torsion-free $\Z_{17}$-module. Then the point-or-cusp Selmer sections of the arithmetic extension with geometric kernel $R$ are exactly the three disjoint rational cusp packets, each parametrized by $H^1(\Q,\Z_{17}(1))$. The assertion includes the full geometric pro-$17$ group, every finite-derived quotient, and every quotient by $\gamma_c$, $c\ge2$, of its ordinary lower central series. No full global section lift or finite ramification support is assumed. More generally, the same conclusion holds with $17$ replaced by any odd regular prime $p>5$ for which \[ a^p+((1-a)\bmod p)^p\equiv1\pmod {p^2},\quad 0\le a<p, \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad a\in\{0,1\}. \] This residue condition is additional to regularity.
depends_on: Milne2006ADT I.3.2-3.5 and I.4.10(b); McCallum1994 Sections3-5; McCallum2001 Lemma1; Washington1982; SGA1 and Wojtkowiak2009

statement: [The remaining prosolvable fibre at seventeen] \label{cor:proseventeen-fibre-intro} Let $n=17^r$, and let $s$ be a prosolvable point-or-cusp Selmer section of $U_n$. Its projection to the full geometric pro-$17$ extension is a cusp section. Choose the full comparison cusp section $t$ lifting that pro-$17$ parameter, and put \[ K_{17}=\ker\bigl(N_n^{\mathrm{sol}}\longrightarrow N_n^{(17)}\bigr). \] With all actions defined by $t$, the natural map identifies $H^1(\Q,K_{17})$ bijectively with the fibre above the distinguished class of $H^1(\Q,N_n^{\mathrm{sol}})\to H^1(\Q,N_n^{(17)})$. The everywhere locally point-or-cusp subset of this fibre remains unclassified. In particular, the preceding theorem does not establish the all-prime prosolvable assertion at exponent seventeen.
depends_on: Milne2006ADT I.3.2-3.5 and I.4.10(b); McCallum1994 Sections3-5; McCallum2001 Lemma1; Washington1982; SGA1 and Wojtkowiak2009

statement: [Fermat sections at exponents with a regular prime factor] \label{thm:regular-solvable-intro} Let \(n\ge3\) be odd and divisible by \(3\), by \(5\), or by a regular prime \(p>5\). For every finite derived quotient \(\Delta/\Delta^{[d]}\), \(d\ge1\), of the geometric fundamental group of \(U_n\), and for its maximal prosolvable quotient, every point-or-cusp Selmer section is cuspidal. The section set is the disjoint union of the three rational cusp packets at \[ [0:1:-1],\qquad [1:0:-1],\qquad [1:-1:0], \] each a torsor under \(H^1(\Q,\widehat\Z(1))\). This includes the geometric abelian and metabelian quotients. The input section need not lift globally to the full fundamental group, and its ramification need not have finite support.
depends_on: cor:all-regular-primary-local; lem:all-regular-compact-boundary; completed Kummer units; filling one cusp; Saidi2022 Propositions3.1/3.2 and TheoremB for the actual full cusp-section action

statement: [The classified prosolvable fibre at seventeen] \label{cor:classified-seventeen-fibre-intro} Let \(n=17^r\), \(r\ge1\), fix a rational cusp \(P\), and fix a parameter \(\beta_{17}\in H^1(\Q,\Z_{17}(1))\). Extend it by zero at the other coefficient primes to \(\widehat\beta\in H^1(\Q,\widehat\Z(1))\), and use the full cusp section \(t_{P,\widehat\beta}\) to define all actions. Put \[ K_{17}=\ker\bigl(N_n^{\mathrm{sol}}\longrightarrow N_n^{(17)}\bigr). \] The natural map identifies \(H^1(\Q,K_{17})\) bijectively with the fibre over the distinguished class of \[ H^1(\Q,N_n^{\mathrm{sol}}) \longrightarrow H^1(\Q,N_n^{(17)}). \] Inside this fibre, the point-or-cusp Selmer subset is exactly the image of the cusp parameters \[ H^1\left(\Q,\prod_{\ell\ne17}\Z_\ell(1)\right). \] Equivalently, the Selmer lifts of the fixed pro-\(17\) cusp section form a torsor under that prime-to-\(17\) completed Kummer group. This identifies a subset of \(H^1(\Q,K_{17})\), not that whole nonabelian cohomology set.
depends_on: thm:regular-solvable-intro; thm:regular-primary-packets-intro; nonabelian cohomology exact fibre and fixed-point vanishing

statement: [The compact local centre at a regular prime] \label{thm:regular-primary-local-intro} Let \(p>5\) be regular, put \(J_p=\Jac(X_p)\), and fix a rational coordinate cusp \(O\). Suppose \[ t\in H^1(\Q,T_pJ_p),\qquad R_v\in X_p(\Q_v)\quad(v<\infty), \qquad \loc_v(t)=\kappa_{p,v}([R_v-O]) \] for every finite place, where \(\kappa_{p,v}\) is the inverse-limit \(p\)-primary Kummer map. Then every permitted \(R_p\) is one of the three rational coordinate cusps. Consequently the same local-centre conclusion holds for any quotient section mapping to the proper geometrically abelian pro-\(p\) quotient and having full local point-or-cusp representatives.
depends_on: cor:irreg-cubic; prop:regular-primary-brauer-cusp-discs; compatible finite Weil-pairing reciprocity

statement: [Geometric pro-prime cusp classification at regular primes] \label{thm:regular-primary-packets-intro} Let \(p>5\) be regular, let \(n=p^r\) with \(r\ge1\), and put \(N_n^{(p)}=\pi_1(U_{n,\overline\Q})^{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}p}\). Let \(R\) be a \(G_\Q\)-stable quotient of \(N_n^{(p)}\) inducing an isomorphism on abelianization, and suppose that every closed ordinary lower-central factor of \(R\) is torsion-free over \(\Z_p\). The point-or-cusp Selmer sections of its arithmetic extension are exactly the three disjoint rational cusp packets, each a torsor under \(H^1(\Q,\Z_p(1))\). This includes the full geometric pro-\(p\) group, every finite-derived quotient, and every quotient by \(\gamma_c\), \(c\ge2\), of the ordinary lower central series. No global full section lift or finite ramification support is assumed.
depends_on: Proper cyclotomic Kummer torsors; McCallum1994 Sections3-5; Milne2006ADT I.3 and I.4.10(b); Washington1982; SGA1; Wojtkowiak2009; integral free-Lie and free-solvable inputs

statement: [Finite cyclotomic first-case obstructions] \label{thm:first-case-obstructions-intro} Let \(p\ge5\), \(K=\Q(\zeta_p)\), and \(r^-=\dim_{\F_p}\Cl(K)[p]^-\). In the model \(F_p:X^p+Y^p=Z^p\), put \(\Delta_p=\pi_1(F_{p,\overline\Q})\). Suppose a section of \[ \pi_1(F_p/\Q)\big/ \overline{[\Delta_p,\Delta_p]\Delta_p^p}\longrightarrow G_\Q \] has at every finite place a representative that is the image of the full proper point section of \(R_v\in F_p(\Q_v)\). If \((r^-+2)(r^-+3)-2<p\), every permitted \(R_p\) reduces to a rational coordinate cusp. More generally, if \(R_p\) has primitive unit coordinates, use the signed coordinates \(a,b,c\) with \(a+b+c=0\) modulo \(p\), and for each ordered pair put \(e=b/(a+b)\in\F_p\). Define \[ C_m(E)=[W^m]\log(1-E+E\exp W)\in\F_p[E], \qquad 3\le m\le p-2, \] with the series truncated through degree \(p-2\). For every odd such \(m\), the direct character convention \(\sigma_i(\zeta_p)=\zeta_p^i\), \(\omega(\sigma_i)=i\), gives \[ \Cl(K)[p]^{(\omega^m)}=0\ \Longrightarrow\ C_m(e)=0, \qquad B_{p-m}C_m(e)=0\quad\hbox{in }\F_p. \] Here \(B_j\) is the \(j\)-th Bernoulli number. In particular \(p\nmid\operatorname{num}(B_{p-3})\) excludes a first-case centre. All these assertions apply to every compatible quotient section with the same full local representatives.
depends_on: Proper finite Kummer torsors; explicit virtual-unit and truncated-log proofs; Gras2010 Sections3.1-3.2; Herbrand1932 Section4; Ribet1976 Theorem1.1 p151 for the forward Herbrand direction; Washington1982 Section6.3

statement: [One fixed finite set of compact local centres] \label{thm:finite-local-centres-intro} Let \(p\ge5\), put \(J_n=\Jac(X_n)\), and use the coordinate cusp \(O=[0:1:-1]\) on each \(X_n\). Suppose \[ r=\dim_{\F_p}\Cl(\Q(\zeta_p))/p\Cl(\Q(\zeta_p)) <\frac{p+3}{8}. \] There is a set \(S_p\subset X_p(\Q_p)\), containing the three rational coordinate cusps and of size at most \(p\), with the following uniform property. For every \[ t\in H^1(\Q,T_pJ_p),\quad R_v\in X_p(\Q_v),\quad \loc_v(t)=\kappa_{p,v}([R_v-O])\quad(v<\infty), \] one has \(R_p\in S_p\); the set is independent of the class and of all its local representatives. At \(p=37,59,67\), these hypotheses hold and \(S_p\) can be chosen inside the three cusp residue discs. For odd \(n=pm\), put \(d=\gcd(m,p-1)\). There is similarly one fixed set \(S_{n,p}\subset X_n(\Q_p)\) containing every centre of a compact \(T_pJ_n\) datum of this form, and every \(\Q_p\)-rational coordinate boundary point, such that \[ |S_{n,p}|\le(p-3)d^2+3d. \] If \(p\) is the least prime factor of \(n\), then \(d=1\), so the bound is \(p\). These are finite-set bounds; equality with the set of rational cusps is not asserted.
depends_on: McCallum2001 Propositions2/3 pp397-398 with complete proofs; Milne2006ADT finite duality/reciprocity; Masley1978 Theorem3.2 p310; Newman1970 Table2 p218; explicit wild quotient and fibre count

[Finite-field boundary fibres] \label{thm:finitefield-boundary-intro} Let \(n\ge3\), let \(k=\F_Q\) have characteristic prime to \(3n\), and let \(C_n:X^n+Y^n+Z^n=0\). Write \(D_X,D_Y,D_Z\) for the coordinate divisors and \(D\) for their disjoint union. Put \[ N=\pi_1(C_{n, ar k})^{\mathrm{pro}	ext{-}3},\qquad \Pi=\pi_1(C_n)/\ker igl(\pi_1(C_{n, ar k})\longrightarrow N igr), \] keeping full \(G_k\) as arithmetic quotient, and let \(\kappa\) be the proper point-section map modulo \(N\)-conjugacy. Points in different coordinate components have distinct classes. If \(D(k)
e\varnothing\), put \(d=\gcd(n,Q-1)\). Each component has \(d\) points, and there is one divisor \(h\mid d\) such that its fibres are cosets of \(\mu_h(k)\) in its regular \(\mu_d(k)\)-action. There are exactly \(3d/h\) boundary classes, and \(3

statement: \label{def:point-cusp-selmer} For any of these arithmetic quotients, a \emph{point-or-cusp Selmer section} is a continuous section, considered modulo geometric conjugacy, whose restriction at every place $v$ is the image either of a point section from $U(k_v)$ or of a section of the decomposition group of a $k_v$-rational point of $D$. We write $\Sec^{\pc}_{\Sel}$ for this set. A global section is \emph{cuspidal} if it factors, up to geometric conjugacy, through the image of the decomposition group of one point of $D(k)$.
depends_on: Definition of the arithmetic quotient retains full Galois group

statement: [Filling one rational cusp]\label{lem:boundary} Suppose $g(X)\geq1$, $\#D(\bar k)\geq2$, and $Q\in D(k)$. The peripheral map \[ H^1(k,\wh\Z(1))\longrightarrow H^1(k,\Delta_1) \] at $Q$ is injective, as are its analogues at every finite completion. Moreover, if every finite localization of a class in $H^1(k,\Delta_1)$ belongs to the peripheral image at $Q$, the global class belongs to that image.
depends_on: Saidi2022 Lemma2.3 and Proposition3.2; boundary homology exact sequence

statement: \label{rem:transfer-scope} The theorem does not use an unrestricted local section conjecture. Nor does it assert that the corresponding statement follows for an arbitrary quotient or from an arbitrary abelian section criterion. The proof uses the full geometric abelianization and a specific localization theorem for the actual derived quotients. These points are essential when comparing with a single-prime quotient.
depends_on: Stoll2007; Saidi2022; arithmetic propositions and separately cited inputs

statement: [Geometric and arithmetic hypotheses] \label{rem:split-prime-scope} The geometric hypothesis holds if $\dim A\ge2$ and the homomorphism $\Jac(X)\to A$ induced by $f$ is surjective: differences of an elliptic translate generate only that elliptic subvariety. Genus at least two of $X$ alone does not exclude an elliptic image. Over any number field, the same initial argument followed directly by Stoll's Theorem~8.2 works if the places whose residue characteristic $\ell$ satisfies $T_\ell\Sha(k,A)=0$ have density one. The completely split criterion avoids imposing that density-one condition over $\Q$ itself. Neither formulation proves the required arithmetic vanishing for a new abelian variety.
depends_on: Stoll2007 Proposition5.16 and Theorem8.2; Stoll2017 erratum; Pila-Zannier2008 Theorem1.1star

statement: \label{prop:lvalue} The root number in \eqref{eq:fe} is $+1$, and the enclosed central value is \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} L(A/\Q,1)=0.7183136284205647705166034780506424+\varepsilon,\\ |\varepsilon|<6.57\cdot10^{-35}. \end{gathered} \label{eq:lvalue} \end{equation} In particular $L(A/\Q,1)>0$.

statement: \label{rem:eleven-factor-only} Only the factor $A_{11}$ is used. The whole Fermat Jacobian $\Jac(X_{11})$ has positive Mordell--Weil rank: its rank is six by \citet[Introduction and \S4]{GrossRohrlich1978}. The target criterion in Stoll's theorem allows this distinction.

statement: [Local source surjectivity]\label{lem:source} If \eqref{eq:sourcecriterion} holds, the natural homomorphism $G_{\Q_3}\to\Gamma_S$ is surjective. Condition \eqref{eq:sourcecriterion} holds for \[ S=\{3\},\qquad S=\{3,7\},\qquad S=\{3,q\}\quad(q\text{ prime},\ q\equiv2\text{ or }5\pmod9). \]

statement: [The compact cubic at three]\label{lem:cubiclocal} For $E:v^2+v=u^3-7$, the group $E(\Q_3)$ is pro-$3$. Its $3$-adic Kummer map is therefore injective. A global class in $H^1(\Q,T_3E)$ that is Kummer at $3$ is the Kummer class of one of the three points of $E(\Q)$.

statement: [Action and change of tangent]\label{lem:action} Let $n=3^r$, $r\geq1$, and put $N=\pi_1((U_n)_{\bar\Q})^{(3)}$. Choose at a rational coordinate cusp the tangent supplied by a coordinate parameter with leading coefficient one. The resulting actual action on $N$ is unramified outside $3$, and its restriction to $G_K$ has pro-$3$ image. The relative cocycle between any two such standard rational tangents is also unramified outside $3$.
depends_on: Shafarevich1963 p82; actual tangential action; exact local Kummer/source calculations; independent cubic isogeny descent; equivariant freeness; pullback/norm and boundary cocycles

statement: [Restricted pro-$3$ Fermat sections]\label{thm:restricted3} Let $n=3^r$, $r\geq1$, and fix one of the standard integral tangents in Lemma~\ref{lem:action}. Let $M=N/J$, where $J$ is a closed Galois-stable normal subgroup of $N$ contained in $[N,N]$; the choice $J=1$ is permitted. Suppose $S$ is a finite set containing $3$ and satisfies \eqref{eq:sourcecriterion}. If a section of $M\rtimes G_\Q$ has its entire relative cocycle trivial on inertia outside $S$ and its localization at $3$ is point-or-cusp geometric, then it is globally cuspidal. statement: [The inherited arithmetic action and its localization] \label{lem:lm-power-action} For a standard integral tangent at any rational cusp of $U_n$, the actual action of $G_{\mathbb Q}$ on $N_n$ factors through \[ \Gamma=\operatorname{Gal}(K_{\{3\}}(3)/\mathbb Q), \qquad K=\mathbb Q(\zeta_3). \] Its restriction to $G_K$ has pro-$3$ image, and the local map $G_{\mathbb Q_3}\to\Gamma$ is surjective. If $M$ is a finite free $\mathbb Z_3$-module with an action obtained from this action by subquotients and tensor operations, then an unramified-outside-$3$ class $a\in H^1(\mathbb Q,M)$ with $a_3=0$ is zero.

statement: [Inertia of a local geometric section] \label{lem:lm-local-inertia} Let $p\ne3$, and let $s_p$ be the image of a full local point or cusp section in the geometrically pro-$3$ fundamental group. Let $J_p$ be arithmetic inertia and let $\tau_p:J_p\to\Z_3(1)$ be the tame $3$-adic character. Relative to an extending tangential origin, its geometric cocycle has the following restriction, up to geometric conjugation: \begin{enumerate} \item If an ordinary local point reduces into the affine special fiber, its restriction to $J_p$ is trivial. \item If an ordinary local point reduces to a boundary point $d$, its restriction has image in a conjugate of cusp inertia $I_d$ and is $\tau_p\mapsto m\tau_p$ there, where $m\in\Z_{>0}$ is its intersection multiplicity with the boundary. \item At a local rational cusp $d$, with parameter $\gamma\in H^1(\Q_p,\Z_3(1))$, its restriction has image in a conjugate of $I_d$ and is $\tau_p\mapsto v_p(\gamma)\tau_p$ there, where $v_p(\gamma)\in\Z_3$ is the completed Kummer valuation. \end{enumerate}

statement: [Compact class and boundary center] \label{lem:lm-power-compact} Let $s$ be a Selmer section of an arithmetic quotient of $\pi_1(U_n)$ which retains $N_n^{\mathrm{ab}}$. Here every local section must be the image of a full point section or a full rational-cusp section. There is a unique rational coordinate cusp $P\in D_n(\mathbb Q)$ with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item Every full local representative at $3$ is cuspidal at $P$. \item The global compact class of $s$ in $H^1(\mathbb Q,T_3J_n)$ is the Kummer class of $P$. \item At every $p\ne3$, any local cusp representative is at $P$, and any ordinary local representative reducing to the boundary reduces to $P$. \end{enumerate}

statement: [Abelian Selmer cuspidality for every power of three] \label{thm:lm-power-abelian} For every $r\ge1$, the Selmer sections with geometric group $N_{3^r}^{\mathrm{ab}}$ are exactly the three disjoint rational cusp packets, each parametrized by $H^1(\mathbb Q,\mathbb Z_3(1))$. Moreover, for any quotient retaining this abelianization, every full local representative at $3$ has the same cusp parameter as this global cusp section. At $p\ne3$ its whole geometric inertia is, up to geometric conjugation, \[ \tau\longmapsto i_P\bigl(v_p(\beta)\tau_p(\tau)\bigr), \qquad \tau\in I_p, \] where $\beta$ is the global parameter and $\tau_p$ is the tame $3$-adic character.

statement: [Infinite support and central differences]\label{rem:infinite-support} Filling the selected cusp kills its entire ramification contribution. There is no general finite-support conclusion for $\beta$. Indeed, \[ H^1(\Q,\Z_3(1))\simeq \varprojlim_m\Q^\times/(\Q^\times)^{3^m} \] identifies with exponent families $(b_p)_p\in\prod_p\Z_3$ such that, for each $m$, only finitely many $b_p$ are nonzero modulo $3^m$. The support itself may be infinite: if $p_1,p_2,\ldots$ enumerate the primes other than $3$, take $b_{p_j}=3^j$ and $b_3=0$. This is an actual global cusp parameter, whose cusp section is Selmer and ramifies at every $p_j$. Thus continuity and local geometry cannot by themselves force the original section into a fixed finite ramification set. If the parameter's support is contained in one of the finite sets for which the arithmetic source is dominated by $G_{\Q_3}$, the inertia formula does place the whole section in that restricted theorem and proves cuspidality. The unrestricted conclusion is proved below by applying the arithmetic-source argument to successive central differences.

In particular there is a natural $G_\Q$-equivariant surjection \[ (N^{\rm ab})^{\otimes m}\longrightarrow L_m. \] Moreover $\bigcap_m\gamma_mN=1$. For any cusp $P$, its inertia $I_P$ is generated by a member of a free pro-$3$ basis of $N$. If $0\ne b\in\Z_3$, then \[ N_N(I_P^{\,b})=I_P. \] Here $I_P^{\,b}$ denotes the image of multiplication by $b$ in $I_P$.

statement: [Why the proof works directly upstairs] \label{rem:lm-derived-cover-obstruction} An open embedding of full pro-$3$ groups need not remain injective after taking derived quotients. Moreover, if $H$ is an open subgroup of a free pro-$3$ group $F$, the quotient $F/H'$ need not have torsion-free ordinary central factors, even though it retains $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$. For example, let $F$ be free on $x,y$ and let $H$ be the kernel of $F\to\mathbb Z/3\mathbb Z$ taking $x$ to $1$ and $y$ to $0$. In $F/H'$, the relation $[x^3,y]=1$ makes $3[x,y]=0$ in the second lower-central factor. The image of $[x,y]$ there is nonzero: map $F$ onto the Heisenberg group over $\mathbb F_3$, where the image of $H$ is abelian and $[x,y]$ is a nontrivial central element. The second lower-central factor is therefore $\mathbb Z/3\mathbb Z$. Consequently a full-group cover argument for $U_{3^r}\to U_3$ does not by itself prove the finite-derived assertion upstairs. statement: [Rank-one factors and integral compact localization] \label{lem:rank-one-compact-localization} Let $D/\mathbb Q$ be an abelian variety with finite $\Sha(D/\mathbb Q)$. Suppose that $D$ is rationally isogenous to a product $\prod_iD_i$ with $\operatorname{rank}D_i(\mathbb Q)\le1$ for every $i$. There is no restriction on the isogeny's degree.

statement: [Compact and affine scope] \label{rem:eleven-compact-scope} This proves the compact localization condition for the base exponent eleven. It does not establish the corresponding condition for $11\cdot3^r$ with $r\ge1$, nor the global cuspidality of all affine pro-three Selmer sections at exponent eleven. In the latter problem, the distinct coordinate cusps have differences of order eleven, so their compact three-adic Kummer classes coincide. The good-place argument that selects one cusp using a nonzero three-primary cusp difference therefore cannot be imported from the exponents divisible by three. Separation of the affine cusp packets at three does not, by itself, impose the needed global boundary support condition.

statement: [A dimension obstruction to a single local arithmetic source] \label{prop:pro3-source-dimension-obstruction} Let $K/\mathbb Q$ be a finite Galois extension containing $\mu_3$, let $d=[K:\mathbb Q]$, and let $t$ be the number of its primes above three. Let $S$ be a finite set of finite primes of $K$, containing all primes above three and stable under $\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb Q)$, and write $s=|S|-t$. For any $v\mid3$ one has \[ \dim_{\mathbb F_3}\ker\left( H^1(G_{K,S},\mathbb F_3)\longrightarrow H^1(K_v,\mathbb F_3) \right) \ge \frac{d(t-2)}{2t}+t+s-2. \] In particular, the homomorphism from $G_{K_v}$ to the maximal pro-three quotient of $G_{K,S}$ cannot be surjective if $t\ge3$, or if $t=2$ and $s>0$. For every such $K$ containing $\mathbb Q(\zeta_{11})$, the second conclusion applies when $S$ contains all primes above both three and eleven. For every such $K$ containing $\mathbb Q(\zeta_{13})$, the first conclusion applies even when $S$ consists only of the primes above three.

statement: [What the obstruction does not say] \label{rem:pro3-source-dimension-scope} This is an obstruction to the particular universal arithmetic-source argument, not to injectivity for a specified geometric coefficient module, and not a construction of a noncuspidal Selmer section. A global $G_{\mathbb Q}$-equivariant cocycle that vanishes at a chosen place also has conjugate local restrictions constrained at the other places above three. Joint localization or an isotypic cohomology calculation can therefore be stronger than the single-place argument tested here. Compact geometric Kummer classes may also be unramified at the exponent prime after potential good reduction, allowing a smaller set $S$. When $t=2$ and $s=0$, the displayed dimension bound is zero and supplies no obstruction.

statement: [The regular-prime cusp residue classes] \label{prop:regular-brauer-cusp-discs} Let $p>5$ be regular, meaning that the class number of $\mathbb Q(\zeta_p)$ is prime to $p$. In each residue class of a rational coordinate cusp, the local zero set $F_p(\mathbb Q_p)^{\operatorname{Br}_{\{p\}}(\mathcal F_p)}$ contains just that cusp. In particular, \[ F_{17}(\mathbb Q_{17})^{\operatorname{Br}_{\{17\}}(\mathcal F_{17})} =D_{17}(\mathbb Q). \]

statement: [Why one place does not give the all-prime theorem] \label{rem:seventeen-global-bridge} The preceding two results do not imply $X_{17}(\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q})_\bullet^{f\text{-}\mathrm{ab}} =X_{17}(\mathbb Q)$. At positive Mordell--Weil rank, a single finite place cannot detect the full profinite Mordell--Weil completion. Indeed $A(\mathbb Q_q)$ has an open pro-$q$ subgroup with finite quotient $G$. For every prime $\ell\ne q$ not dividing $|G|$, its $\ell$-adic completion is zero, whereas $A(\mathbb Q)^{\wedge}$ contains $\mathbb Z_\ell^{\operatorname{rank}A(\mathbb Q)}$. The same obstruction applies to any fixed finite collection of local places. There is also a curve-level distinction. Given a rational point $O$ on a smooth proper curve, fix a good prime $q\ne p$ and choose a different $Q_q$ sufficiently close to $O$. The Abel--Jacobi difference lies in the pro-$q$ formal subgroup, where multiplication by $p$ is an automorphism. The adelic point equal to $O$ except for the component $Q_q$ therefore has trivial compact $p$-adic Kummer class at every place and survives every $p$-primary finite abelian torsor. It need not be diagonal. This is a limitation of the single-primary condition, not a counterexample to full finite abelian descent. Stoll's Theorem~8.2 requires finite support at a density-one set of places; the one place seventeen does not meet that hypothesis after a finite number-field extension.

statement: [A sufficient criterion allowing positive rank] \label{prop:positive-rank-split-prime-criterion} Let $X/\mathbb Q$ be a smooth proper curve of genus at least one, with rational base point $O$. Let $f:X\to A$ be a morphism to an abelian variety and $Z\subset X$ a finite $\mathbb Q$-subscheme. Suppose that there is a finite Galois extension $L/\mathbb Q$ such that, for all but finitely many rational primes $\ell$ split completely in $L$, \[ T_\ell\Sha(A/\mathbb Q)=0 \] and \[ \{x\in X(\mathbb Q_\ell): \log_\ell(f(x)-f(O))\in \operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q_\ell} \log_\ell A(\mathbb Q)\} \subset Z(\mathbb Q_\ell). \] Then $X(\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q})_\bullet^{f\text{-}\mathrm{ab}} =X(\mathbb Q)\subset Z(\mathbb Q)$.

statement: \label{prop:conjugate-source-not-enough} There exist a profinite group \(\Gamma=P\rtimes\Delta\), with \(P\) a finitely generated free pro-three group and \(|\Delta|\) prime to three, a closed subgroup \(D\), and a finite free continuous \(\mathbf Z_3[\Gamma]\)-module \(T\), such that: \begin{enumerate} \item the image of \(P\) on \(T\) is pro-three; \item the conjugates of \(D\) generate \(\Gamma\); \item \(T^D=0\); \item \(H^1(\Gamma,T)\longrightarrow H^1(D,T)\) is not injective, even after tensoring with \(\mathbf Q_3\). \end{enumerate} The same nonzero class restricts to zero on every conjugate of \(D\).

statement: [A module-specific sufficient condition] \label{lem:source-local-parameter} Let \(\Gamma=P\rtimes\Delta\), with \(P\) pro-three and \(\Delta\) finite of order prime to three. Let \(D=P_0\rtimes\Delta_0\) be a closed subgroup, where \(\Delta_0\subset\Delta\), and suppose the \(\Delta\)-conjugates of \(P_0\) generate \(P\). If \(T\) is finite free over \(\mathbf Z_3\) and \(T^{P_0}=0\), there is a natural injection \[ \ker\!\left(H^1(\Gamma,T)\to H^1(D,T)\right) \hookrightarrow T^{\Delta_0}/T^\Delta. \] In particular equality of the two invariant lattices implies localization injectivity.

statement: [The exact local-parameter condition] \label{prop:source-exact-relation-condition} Let \(\Gamma=P\rtimes\Delta\), where \(P\) is pro-three and \(\Delta\) is finite of order prime to three. Let \(D=P_0\rtimes\Delta_0\), with \(\Delta_0\subset\Delta\), be a closed subgroup. Suppose the \(\Delta\)-conjugates of \(P_0\) generate \(P\). Let \(T\) be a finite free continuous \(\mathbf Z_3[\Gamma]\)-module with \(T^{P_0}=0\). Form the free pro-three product \(F\) of copies of \(P_0\) indexed by \(\Delta/\Delta_0\), with the action induced by the conjugation action of \(\Delta_0\) on \(P_0\). The conjugation maps give a surjection \(F\to P\). Put \(R=\ker(F\to P)\). For \(b\in T^{\Delta_0}\), let \(c_b\) be the cocycle on \(F\) whose restriction to the factor indexed by \(\sigma\Delta_0\) is the coboundary with parameter \(\sigma b\). Then \begin{equation} \ker\!\left(H^1(\Gamma,T)\longrightarrow H^1(D,T)\right) \simeq \frac{\{b\in T^{\Delta_0}:c_b|_R=0\}}{T^\Delta}. \label{eq:source-exact-relation-condition} \end{equation}

statement: [An abelian-character localization condition] \label{prop:cm-character-localization-condition} Let \(E/\mathbf Q\) be finite Galois. Let \(S\) be a finite set of rational primes containing three and the ramification of \(E/\mathbf Q\) and of a finite-dimensional continuous \(\mathbf Q_3\)-representation \(V\). Let \(E_S\) be the maximal extension of \(E\) unramified outside the primes over \(S\). Suppose \(E_\infty\subset E_S\) is Galois over \(\mathbf Q\), is abelian over \(E\), and trivializes the action of \(G_E\) on \(V\). Put \[ H=\operatorname{Gal}(E_\infty/E),\qquad \Delta=\operatorname{Gal}(E/\mathbf Q). \] Suppose that, over a finite coefficient extension \(\Omega/\mathbf Q_3\), the \(H\)-representation \(V_\Omega=V\otimes_{\mathbf Q_3}\Omega\) is a direct sum of characters, each nontrivial on \(H\) and on every local decomposition image \(H_v\) for \(v\mid3\). Let \(X_S^{[3]}(E_\infty)\) be the maximal abelian pro-three quotient of \(\operatorname{Gal}(E_S/E_\infty)\) in which the decomposition groups at every prime above three vanish. Thus it classifies abelian pro-three extensions unramified outside \(S\) and split at every three-adic prime. There is a natural isomorphism \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\ker\!\left(H^1(G_{\mathbf Q,S},V) \longrightarrow H^1(\mathbf Q_3,V)\right) \otimes_{\mathbf Q_3}\Omega\\ &\qquad\simeq \operatorname{Hom}^{\mathrm{cts}}_H \bigl(X_S^{[3]}(E_\infty),V_\Omega\bigr)^\Delta. \end{split} \label{eq:cm-character-localization-condition} \end{equation} In particular only the character components which occur in \(V_\Omega\) need to vanish.

statement: [Integral recovery from rational injectivity] \label{lem:localization-integral-recovery} Let \(T\) be a stable finite free \(\mathbf Z_3\)-lattice in \(V\), and assume \(V^{G_{\mathbf Q_3}}=0\). If \[ H^1(G_{\mathbf Q,S},V)\longrightarrow H^1(\mathbf Q_3,V) \] is injective, then so is the corresponding map with coefficients in \(T\).

statement: [Local nontriviality for the eleven coefficient characters] \label{lem:eleven-coefficient-local-nontriviality} Let \(N_{11}\) be the geometric pro-three group of \(U_{11}\), and put \(E=\mathbf Q(\zeta_{11})\). Over a finite splitting coefficient field, every character in a positive ordinary lower-central grade of \(N_{11}\) is nontrivial on \(G_{E_v}\) for each \(v\mid3\). The same holds for every nonzero character in a stable quotient of such a grade. In particular these rational coefficient modules have zero local invariants at three.

statement: [A degree-two boundary component] \label{rem:boundary-finite-invariant-obstruction} For \(a=11\) or \(13\), put \(E=\mathbf Q(\zeta_a)\). The boundary module of \(U_a\) has the integral decomposition \[ B_a\simeq\mathbf Z_3(1)^2\oplus \left(\operatorname{Ind}_{G_E}^{G_{\mathbf Q}} \mathbf Z_3(1)\right)^3. \] There are three rational boundary points and three primitive cyclotomic orbits; eliminating one rational basis vector proves the decomposition. Coordinate-cusp differences are killed by \(a\), so the generalized-Jacobian extension splits on three-adic Tate modules. Hence \(B_a\) is a summand of the geometric abelian module. For the free geometric pro-three group, its second lower-central grade is the exterior square of that module. Choose a nontrivial character \(\eta\) of \((\mathbf Z/a)^\times/\langle3\rangle\), using a coefficient extension when necessary. Bracketing a rational boundary line with the \(\eta\)-line in an induced summand gives \(\Omega(2)\otimes\eta\) in the second grade. For eleven one can take the odd quadratic character; for thirteen the displayed quotient is \(C_4\). The finite character \(\eta\) is trivial on the local group at three and nontrivial globally. The square of the finite mod-three cyclotomic character is trivial. Thus the associated finite coefficient representation has more local invariants than global invariants already in degree two. An invariant-equality criterion alone cannot handle all these grades. This does not establish a nonzero localization kernel: the relation condition or the arithmetic character condition must still be tested.

statement: [Finite ramification and the base-exponent problem] \label{rem:joint-localization-ramification-scope} The character condition concerns classes in \(H^1(G_{\mathbf Q,S},V)\). It does not force an arbitrary affine Selmer section to have its whole relative cocycle unramified outside \(S\). At a prime exponent different from three, compact three-adic Kummer classes do not detect differences between coordinate cusps, since those differences have order prime to three. Compact localization and one locally cuspidal representative therefore do not by themselves restrict boundary ramification to one global cusp direction. If the global abelian class is already that of one cusp, the point-or-cusp local condition can control inertia in the subsequent central induction. A nonzero boundary inertia vector forces the same cusp direction; a zero vector makes the whole inertia trivial. This is a separate step, preceding application of a finite-ramification cohomological condition. The propositions above consequently supply formal module-specific conditions, not a new base-eleven or base-thirteen pro-three cuspidality theorem.

statement: [The rational factors and their rank bounds] \label{prop:thirtyone-rational-factors} There is a rational isogeny $J\sim_\Q A\times P$, where $\dim A=5$, $\dim P=10$, and \[ \operatorname{End}^0_\Q(J)=\Q\times\Q(\zeta_3),\qquad \operatorname{End}^0_\Q(A)=\Q,\qquad \operatorname{End}^0_\Q(P)=\Q(\zeta_3). \] Both factors are $\Q$-simple, and \[ \operatorname{rank}A(\Q)\ge1,\qquad \operatorname{rank}J(\Q)\le4,\qquad \operatorname{rank}P(\Q)\in\{0,2\}. \] Thus $P$ is the only possible positive-dimensional rational rank-zero isogeny factor of this particular $J$.

statement: [The central vanishing and the cubic-character restriction] \label{prop:thirtyone-central-obstruction} The whole-Jacobian function has root number $+1$ and \[ L(J/\Q,1)=L'(J/\Q,1)=L(A/\Q,1)=0. \] If $\chi$ is a cubic Dirichlet character modulo $31$, then, over a coefficient field containing its values, \[ V(J)=V(A)\oplus V(A)\otimes\chi\oplus V(A)\otimes\chi^2. \] The two complementary weight-two Hilbert constituents over $F_0$ have nontrivial cubic central characters. statement: [The local parameter at seventeen]\label{rem:frey-three-seventeen-parameter} Near the coordinate cusp \(\lambda=0\), put \(t=X/Z\). The Legendre \(j\)-invariant and its Tate parameter give \[ j=256\frac{(1-\lambda+\lambda^2)^3} {\lambda^2(1-\lambda)^2}, \qquad q_E=2^{-8}t^{34}(1+O(t^{17})). \] Consequently, up to the fixed quadratic twist, the 3-adic extension parameter for a tangential section is \[ \kappa_3(2^{-8})+34\alpha_3. \] The coefficient 34 is a unit in \(\mathbb Z_3\). Thus the Fermat exponent does not annihilate residual 3-adic tame monodromy. In the usual exponent-prime Frey argument the corresponding divisibility kills the residual inertia; that step has no analogue here. At \(\mathbb Q_{17}\), the pro-3 completion of the unit group is zero, since its finite part has order 16 and its principal-unit group is pro-17. Thus \(H^1(\mathbb Q_{17},\mathbb Z_3(1))\cong\mathbb Z_3\) by the valuation, and the constant term vanishes. Multiplication by 34 is an automorphism. Local cuspidality at 17 therefore permits every 3-adic Tate extension parameter; it gives a local invariant line, with no global invariant line and no vanishing of local monodromy forced by this calculation. There is a concrete illustration of this distinction at the representation level. The rational Legendre curve with \(\lambda=17\) has full rational 2-torsion and split multiplicative reduction at 17. Its 3-adic local representation there occurs in a cusp packet by the preceding surjectivity. Yet its mod-3 representation has no global stable line: its 3-division polynomial is \[ 3x^4-72x^3+102x^2-289. \] Modulo 5 its values at \(0,1,2,3,4\) are \(1,4,1,3,3\), so it has no rational root, hence no rational cyclic 3-isogeny. This is not claimed to arise from a Selmer section on \(U_{17}\); it only refutes the implication from the local Tate shape at 17, determinant, and full 2-torsion alone to global residual reducibility. Continuity gives finite ramification separately for each \(3^m\)-torsion representation. It does not give a common finite ramification set for the inverse limit. \citet[Theorem~1]{KhareRajan2001} prove density zero, rather than finiteness, for ramification of semisimple \(p\)-adic representations. \citet[Main Theorem and Remark~1, author p.~3]{KhareLarsenRamakrishna2005} construct, for coefficient primes at least 5, infinitely ramified representations that are potentially semistable at the coefficient prime and pure and rational at almost all unramified primes. Their result is a counterexample to that general shortcut; its stated prime restriction means it is not itself a 3-adic or section-theoretic counterexample. Nor does the finite-level modular curve associated only with a stable line modulo 3 finish the argument. With full 2-torsion it gives level 12, whose modular curve has genus zero. The order-9 subgroup used above gives level 36 and is a strictly stronger condition.

statement: [Nonabelian localization from a surjective arithmetic source]\label{prop:nonabelian-source-localization} Let $S$ contain $3$, let $K/\mathbb Q$ be finite Galois and unramified outside $S$, and put $\Gamma=\operatorname{Gal}(K_S(3)/\mathbb Q)$. Suppose that the image of $G_{\mathbb Q_3}$ in $\Gamma$ is $\Gamma$. Let $M$ be a finitely generated pro-$3$ group with continuous actual $G_{\mathbb Q,S}$-action factoring through $\Gamma$, whose restriction to $G_K$ has pro-$3$ image in $\operatorname{Aut}(M)$. Then \[ H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,S},M)\longrightarrow H^1(\mathbb Q_3,M) \] is injective as a map of nonabelian cohomology sets.

statement: [The full compact image at the base quintic and septic]\label{cor:compact-full-base-five-seven} Let $a\in\{5,7\}$. Every point-or-cusp Selmer section of the full geometrically pro-$3$ arithmetic fundamental group of $U_a$ has compact image globally conjugate to the proper point section of the rational coordinate cusp determined by its localization at $3$. More generally, for any stable quotient $R$ of the affine geometric group retaining its abelianization, the same holds in the compact quotient of $R$, obtained by killing all boundary inertia images.

statement: \label{rem:compact-cusp-frobenius-fibre} At a good prime $p\ne3$, an affine local representative ramifying at a coordinate cusp $Q$ has the proper Frobenius section of $Q$. The corollary therefore restricts such $Q$ to the fibre of the proper geometrically pro-$3$ point map containing $P$. It does not assert that this fibre is a singleton. In particular, coordinate-cusp differences are prime-to-$3$ torsion, so their proper abelian pro-$3$ classes coincide. A finite-field separation statement or a boundary-support argument remains necessary for the affine conclusion. The partial separation proved in Theorem~\ref{thm:finitefield-boundary-intro} leaves precisely the same-component alternative at split fields.

statement: [Density-one Kummer localization]\label{lem:density-one-kummer-localization} Let \(F\) be a number field. Localization on any density-one set of its finite places, in Dirichlet density, is injective on \(H^1(F,\mathbf Z_3(1))\). The analogous statement over \(\mathbf Q\) holds for finite direct sums of induced Tate modules \(\operatorname{Ind}_{G_F}^{G_{\mathbf Q}}\mathbf Z_3(1)\).

statement: \label{lem:frey-rank-one-weights} Let \(\psi:G_L\to E^\times\) be a continuous character of a number field, where \(E/\Q_\ell\) is finite. If it is Hodge--Tate at all places over \(\ell\), then it has finite ramification and is the \(\ell\)-adic realization of an algebraic character of a Serre group \(S_{\mathfrak m}\), defined over a number field. It has realizations at every coefficient prime. For some integer \(b\), at every place \(v\) outside its modulus and different from the coefficient prime its algebraic Frobenius value has absolute value \((Nv)^{b/2}\) under every complex embedding.

statement: \label{prop:frey-weight-open-image} Let \(\rho:G_\Q\to\operatorname{GL}_2(\Q_\ell)\) be continuous, with \(\det\rho=\chi_\ell\), and Hodge--Tate at \(\ell\). Assume that at a density-one set of unramified rational primes \(q\) its polynomial is \(T^2-a_qT+q\), with \(a_q\in\Z\) and both complex roots of absolute value \(q^{1/2}\). If, for one \(r\ne\ell\), \[ (\rho|_{G_{\Q_r}})^{\mathrm{ss}}\simeq\delta\chi_\ell\oplus\delta \quad\text{with }\delta^2=1, \] then \(\rho\) has open image.

statement: [Local Fermat points and the remaining scope] \label{rem:auxiliary-level27-local-fermat} These collisions persist on actual local points of the level cover of \(U_a\), for \(a=5\) or \(7\). At any of the preceding primes \(q\ne a\), take \(w=q^{-m}\) with \(m\ge1\), and set \[ \lambda=w^{3a},\qquad h=\frac{9w^a}{1-w^a}. \] As \(m\) increases, \(h\) approaches \(-9\). Since \(f'\) is a unit at the chosen residue root, the implicit function theorem gives a point of \(C(\Q_q)\) near \(R_q\) with this value of \(h\). Its Kummer class remains that of \(A\). At the same time, \[ x_F=w^3,\qquad y_F=-w^3(1-w^{-3a})^{1/a} \] are defined over \(\Q_q\) by Hensel's lemma and satisfy \(x_F^a+y_F^a=1\), hence give the points \([x_F:y_F:-1]\) of the all-plus model of \(U_a\). They reduce to the coordinate cusp \((1:-1:0)\), where \(\lambda=\infty\). The modular point supplies the cyclic level-\(27\) subgroup for \(\mathcal E_\lambda\); away from the exceptional \(j\)-values, quadratic twisting does not change the field of definition of such a subgroup. Thus the auxiliary \(X_0(27)\) Kummer condition does not separate this boundary from either rational cusp class, even after deleting a finite set of primes. This is a calculation about that condition only. It does not construct a global Selmer section, and it does not identify the full compact pro-$3$ section of \(X_a\) at this boundary with the prescribed rational cusp. The latter finite-field fibre condition remains an additional, unresolved requirement.

statement: [The regular-prime cusp residue classes] \label{prop:regular-primary-brauer-cusp-discs} Let $p>5$ be regular, meaning that the class number of $\mathbb Q(\zeta_p)$ is prime to $p$. In each residue class of a rational coordinate cusp, the local zero set $F_p(\mathbb Q_p)^{\operatorname{Br}_{\{p\}}(\mathcal F_p)[p^\infty]}$ contains just that cusp. In particular, \[ F_{17}(\mathbb Q_{17})^{\operatorname{Br}_{\{17\}}(\mathcal F_{17})[17^\infty]} =D_{17}(\mathbb Q). \]

statement: [Finite-primary reciprocity]\label{lem:finite-primary-reciprocity} Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $A/k$ be an abelian variety over a number field, and let $z\in H^1(k,T_pA)$ have local Kummer representatives $P_v\in A(k_v)^{\wedge_p}$. statement: [The primary local cusp condition] \label{cor:seventeen-primary-local} Let $z\in H^1(\Q,T_{17}J_{17})$ be locally the Kummer class of $[x_v-O]$, with $x_v\in X_{17}(\Q_v)$ and a fixed rational coordinate cusp $O$. statement: [The regular-prime arithmetic source] \label{prop:regular-nonabelian-localization} Let $p$ be odd with $p\nmid h(K)$, where $K=\Q(\zeta_p)$, and let $n=p^r$, $r\ge1$. Put $N_n=\pi_1(U_{n,\overline\Q})^{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}p}$ and $C_n=\pi_1(X_{n,\overline\Q})^{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}p}$. For a standard rational tangent the actual actions on these and all their stable quotients factor through $\Gamma=\Gal(K_{\{p\}}(p)/\Q)$, where $K_{\{p\}}(p)$ is the maximal pro-$p$ extension unramified outside the sole prime above $p$. Their $G_K$-images are pro-$p$, and $G_{\Q_p}\to\Gamma$ is surjective. For every finitely generated pro-$p$ group $M$ with such an action, \[ H^1(G_{\Q,\{p\}},M)\longrightarrow H^1(\Q_p,M) \] is injective as a map of nonabelian cohomology sets. Localization is consequently injective on proper point-local Selmer sections for every stable quotient of $C_n$, and on $H^1(G_{\Q,\{p\}},T_pJ_n)$ and its compact Selmer subgroup.

statement: [Why one place does not give the all-prime theorem] \label{rem:regular-all-prime-limitation} The primary local condition and nonabelian localization do not imply $X_{17}(\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q})_\bullet^{f\text{-}\mathrm{ab}} =X_{17}(\mathbb Q)$. At positive Mordell--Weil rank, a single finite place cannot detect the full profinite Mordell--Weil completion. Indeed $A(\mathbb Q_q)$ has an open pro-$q$ subgroup with finite quotient $G$. For every prime $\ell\ne q$ not dividing $|G|$, its $\ell$-adic completion is zero, whereas $A(\mathbb Q)^{\wedge}$ contains $\mathbb Z_\ell^{\operatorname{rank}A(\mathbb Q)}$. The same obstruction applies to any fixed finite collection of local places. There is also a curve-level distinction. Given a rational point $O$ on a smooth proper curve, fix a good prime $q\ne p$ and choose a different $Q_q$ sufficiently close to $O$. The Abel--Jacobi difference lies in the pro-$q$ formal subgroup, where multiplication by $p$ is an automorphism. The adelic point equal to $O$ except for the component $Q_q$ therefore has trivial compact $p$-adic Kummer class at every place and survives every $p$-primary finite abelian torsor. It need not be diagonal. This is a limitation of the single-primary condition, not a counterexample to full finite abelian descent. Stoll's Theorem~8.2 requires finite support at a density-one set of places; the one place seventeen does not meet that hypothesis after a finite number-field extension.

statement: [Compact cancellation and boundary centers] \label{lem:regular-compact-boundary} Let $s$ be a quotient Selmer section retaining $N_n^{\mathrm{ab}}$. There is a unique rational coordinate cusp $P$ such that every full local witness at $p$ is a cusp witness at $P$ and the global compact abelian class equals that of $P$. At every finite $q\ne p$, each local cusp witness has center $P$, and each ordinary local witness reducing to the boundary reduces to $P$.

statement: [The global abelian cusp parameter] \label{lem:regular-abelian-packet} The abelian Selmer section is the image of one global cusp section $t_{P,\beta}$, with unique $\beta\in H^1(\Q,\Z_p(1))$. Its parameter equals that of every full local cusp witness at $p$. At $q\ne p$, the whole geometric inertia of a full local pro-$p$ witness is, up to conjugacy, $i_P(v_q(\beta)\tau_q)$, where $\tau_q$ is the tame pro-$p$ character.

statement: [Free pro-$p$ groups and positive-weight fixed points] \label{lem:regular-group-fixed-points} The group $N_n$ is free pro-$p$ of rank $n^2+1$, and each cusp inertia is generated by a free basis element. Its ordinary lower-central factors are finite free $\Z_p$-modules and form the free graded Lie algebra. For nonzero $b\in\Z_p$, $N_{N_n}(I_P^b)=I_P$. If a quotient $R$ retains $N_n^{\mathrm{ab}}$ and all its ordinary factors $L_m=\gamma_mR/\gamma_{m+1}R$ are torsion-free, then for $t=t_{P,\beta}$ and every finite place $v$, \[ L_m^{G_{\Q_v}}=0,\qquad (R/\gamma_mR)^{t(G_{\Q_v})}=1,\qquad R^{t(G_\Q)}=1. \] The full group, its finite ordinary-central quotients and its finite-derived quotients satisfy the factor hypothesis.

statement: [Regular-prime cusp packets] \label{thm:regular-prime-packets} Assume $p>5$ is regular and satisfies \eqref{eq:regular-residue-condition}, and let $n=p^r$, $r\ge1$. This includes the full group, every finite ordinary-central quotient retaining abelianization and every finite-derived quotient.

statement: [The remaining prosolvable cohomology fibre] \label{cor:proseventeen-kernel-fibre} Let $n=17^r$, $r\ge1$, write $N_n^{\mathrm{sol}}$ for the maximal geometric prosolvable group, and put $K_{17}=\ker(N_n^{\mathrm{sol}}\to N_n)$. Extend $\beta_{17}$ by zero at other primes to $\widehat\beta$, and use its global prosolvable cusp section $\widehat t$ as origin. Then \[ H^1(\Q,K_{17})\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \operatorname{fib}_{1}\bigl(H^1(\Q,N_n^{\mathrm{sol}}) \longrightarrow H^1(\Q,N_n)\bigr), \] where all actions are induced by $\widehat t$. The original Selmer condition defines a subset of this fibre; no vanishing or classification of that subset is asserted.

statement: \label{lem:irreg-virtual} There is an exact sequence of \(\F_p[\Delta]\)-modules \begin{equation} 0\longrightarrow E_K/E_K^p \longrightarrow V \longrightarrow\Cl(K)[p]\longrightarrow0. \label{eq:irreg-virtual} \end{equation} Consequently, if \(r^-=\dim_{\F_p}\Cl(K)[p]^-\), then \begin{equation} \dim_{\F_p}V^-=1+r^-. \label{eq:irreg-minus-dim} \end{equation} For odd \(m\) with \(3\leq m\leq p-2\), \begin{equation} V^{(\omega^m)}\simeq\Cl(K)[p]^{(\omega^m)}. \label{eq:irreg-odd-components} \end{equation}

statement: \label{lem:irreg-proper-torsors} The section supplies classes \[ \xi_i\in H^1(K,\mu_p)=K^\times/K^{\times p} \] satisfying \(\xi_i=\sigma_i\xi_1\) for \(i\neq0\). If that centre has signed coordinates \(a,b,c\) and \(e=b/(a+b)\), then \begin{equation} \loc_{\mathfrak p}(\xi_i) =[1-e+e\zeta_p^i]\in L^\times/L^{\times p}. \label{eq:irreg-local-values} \end{equation} Here \(\mathfrak p\) is the unique prime of \(K\) above \(p\).

Then \begin{equation} \frac{F'(T)}{F(T)}=0 \quad\text{in}\quad \F_p[T,\text{denominators}^{-1}]/(T-1)^p. \label{eq:irreg-derivative} \end{equation}

statement: \label{lem:irreg-k-independent} Suppose \(e,1-e,1-2e\in\Z_p^\times\), and let \(k\geq1\) satisfy \begin{equation} k(k+1)-2<p. \label{eq:irreg-k-bound} \end{equation} Then the classes \[ d_i= \left[\frac{1-e+e\zeta_p^i}{1-e+e\zeta_p^{-i}}\right], \qquad 1\leq i\leq k, \] are linearly independent in \(L^\times/L^{\times p}\).
