statement: \label{thm:irreg-rank} Under the hypotheses of Section~\ref{sec:irreg-setup}, if \begin{equation} (r^-+2)(r^-+3)-2<p, \qquad r^-=\dim_{\F_p}\Cl(K)[p]^-, \label{eq:irreg-rank-bound} \end{equation} then no permitted \(p\)-local centre is first case.
depends_on: Proper finite Kummer torsors; explicit virtual-unit and truncated-log proofs; Gras2010 Sections3.1-3.2; Herbrand1932 Section4; Ribet1976 Theorem1.1 p151 for the forward Herbrand direction; Washington1982 Section6.3

statement: \label{cor:irreg-residue} Under \eqref{eq:irreg-rank-bound}, every permitted \(p\)-local centre reduces to one of \(Q_0,Q_1,Q_\infty\).
depends_on: Proper finite Kummer torsors; explicit virtual-unit and truncated-log proofs; Gras2010 Sections3.1-3.2; Herbrand1932 Section4; Ribet1976 Theorem1.1 p151 for the forward Herbrand direction; Washington1982 Section6.3

statement: \label{thm:irreg-characters} Suppose that a section as in Section~\ref{sec:irreg-setup} has a first-case \(p\)-local centre. For each ordered pair of its signed coordinates, put \(e=b/(a+b)\bmod p\). For every odd integer \(3\leq m\leq p-2\), \begin{equation} \Cl(K)[p]^{(\omega^m)}=0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad C_m(e)=0. \label{eq:irreg-character-zero} \end{equation} In particular, without a class-component hypothesis, \begin{equation} B_{p-m}\,C_m(e)=0\quad\text{in }\F_p. \label{eq:irreg-Bernoulli-congruence} \end{equation}
depends_on: Proper finite Kummer torsors; explicit virtual-unit and truncated-log proofs; Gras2010 Sections3.1-3.2; Herbrand1932 Section4; Ribet1976 Theorem1.1 p151 for the forward Herbrand direction; Washington1982 Section6.3

statement: \label{rem:irreg-endpoint} The proof includes \(m=p-2\). In that case \(\mathcal O_L/(\lambda^{m+1})\) has characteristic \(p\) and length \(p-1\), and no denominator divisible by \(p\) occurs. The logarithm used above is a polynomial on a nilpotent ideal. It is not the \(p\)-adic logarithm of \(\zeta_p\), which is zero. The reflected character \(\omega^{1-m}\) in the usual notation for Mirimanoff polynomials is likewise not the direct character of \(V\) used here. The classical rational-point congruences are treated in \cite[Theorems 3.5 and 3.7]{Gras2010}; the proper-torsor construction above establishes their applicability under the stated quotient hypotheses.
depends_on: Proper finite Kummer torsors; explicit virtual-unit and truncated-log proofs; Gras2010 Sections3.1-3.2; Herbrand1932 Section4; Ribet1976 Theorem1.1 p151 for the forward Herbrand direction; Washington1982 Section6.3

statement: \label{cor:irreg-cubic} If \(\Cl(K)[p]^{(\omega^3)}=0\), no section under consideration has a first-case \(p\)-local centre. In particular it suffices that \begin{equation} p\nmid\operatorname{num}(B_{p-3}). \label{eq:irreg-cubic-condition} \end{equation}
depends_on: Proper finite Kummer torsors; explicit virtual-unit and truncated-log proofs; Gras2010 Sections3.1-3.2; Herbrand1932 Section4; Ribet1976 Theorem1.1 p151 for the forward Herbrand direction; Washington1982 Section6.3

statement: \label{cor:irreg-multiples} Let \(n\) be an odd multiple of \(p\). The rank criterion, the odd-character congruences, and the cubic corollary apply to sections on \(U_n\) whose geometric quotient retains the pullbacks of the proper mod-\(p\) abelian torsors on \(F_p\), with full \(G_\Q\) and full local point-or-cusp representatives. In particular they apply to its geometrically maximal prosolvable arithmetic fundamental group.
depends_on: Proper finite Kummer torsors; explicit virtual-unit and truncated-log proofs; Gras2010 Sections3.1-3.2; Herbrand1932 Section4; Ribet1976 Theorem1.1 p151 for the forward Herbrand direction; Washington1982 Section6.3

statement: [The regular-prime local cusp condition] \label{cor:all-regular-primary-local} Let \(p>5\) be regular, and let \(t\in H^1(\Q,T_pJ_p)\) have localizations \(\kappa_{p,v}([R_v-Q_0])\) for points \(R_v\in F_p(\Q_v)\) at every finite place. Then every permitted \(R_p\) is one of the three rational coordinate cusps. The same conclusion holds for every quotient Selmer section that maps to the proper geometrically abelian pro-\(p\) quotient and has full local point-or-cusp representatives.
depends_on: cor:irreg-cubic; prop:regular-primary-brauer-cusp-discs; compatible finite Weil-pairing reciprocity

statement: [All-prime cusp packets at regular exponents] \label{thm:allprime-regular-bridge} Suppose that \(n\) is divisible by \(3\), by \(5\), or by an odd regular prime \(p>5\). For every \(d\geq1\), and for the maximal geometrically prosolvable quotient, every point-or-cusp Selmer section is cuspidal. After choosing one rational tangent at each rational coordinate point, its section set is \begin{equation} \coprod_{P\in\{P_0,P_1,P_\infty\}} H^1(\mathbb Q,\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1)). \label{eq:allprime-packets} \end{equation} Each displayed packet maps injectively to the section set, and the three images are disjoint. Every permitted full local representative at a finite place has the same rational coordinate centre as its global packet. No common finite ramification set is required for the section or its cusp parameter.
depends_on: cor:all-regular-primary-local; lem:all-regular-compact-boundary; completed Kummer units; filling one cusp; Saidi2022 Propositions3.1/3.2 and TheoremB for the actual full cusp-section action

statement: [Valuations and local Kummer maps] \label{lem:allprime-kummer} The common kernel of all completed valuations \[ v_q:\widehat{\mathbb Q^\times}\longrightarrow\widehat{\mathbb Z} \qquad(q\text{ a rational prime}) \] is \(\{1,-1\}\). Multiplication by any odd positive integer is injective on \(\widehat{\mathbb Q^\times}\). For every finite place \(v\), the map from \(\mathbb Q_v^\times\) to its full power completion is injective. For an abelian variety \(A/\mathbb Q_v\), the map \[ A(\mathbb Q_v)\longrightarrow \varprojlim_N A(\mathbb Q_v)/N A(\mathbb Q_v) \] is injective as well.
depends_on: cor:all-regular-primary-local; lem:all-regular-compact-boundary; completed Kummer units; filling one cusp; Saidi2022 Propositions3.1/3.2 and TheoremB for the actual full cusp-section action

statement: [Recovering a full global cusp parameter] \label{lem:allprime-one-cusp} Let \(X/\mathbb Q\) be a smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at least one, let \(D\) be a reduced finite divisor with at least two geometric points, and put \(U=X\setminus D\). Let \(P\in D(\mathbb Q)\). Suppose a section of a finite full-geometric derived quotient, or of the maximal geometrically prosolvable quotient, has at every finite place a full local cusp representative at \(P\). Then it is the image of a unique full global cusp section at \(P\), where uniqueness refers to its \(H^1(\mathbb Q,\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1))\) parameter after a rational tangent has been chosen.
depends_on: cor:all-regular-primary-local; lem:all-regular-compact-boundary; completed Kummer units; filling one cusp; Saidi2022 Propositions3.1/3.2 and TheoremB for the actual full cusp-section action

statement: [From one primary cusp to all finite centres] \label{prop:allprime-base-regular} Let \(p>5\) be regular. Every section satisfying the local condition on \(U_p\), in any quotient in Theorem~\ref{thm:allprime-regular-bridge}, has all its full finite local witnesses cuspidal at one rational coordinate point.
depends_on: cor:all-regular-primary-local; lem:all-regular-compact-boundary; completed Kummer units; filling one cusp; Saidi2022 Propositions3.1/3.2 and TheoremB for the actual full cusp-section action

statement: [Odd-multiple transfer] \label{prop:allprime-odd-transfer} Let \(a\geq3\) be odd, and suppose that the conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:allprime-regular-bridge} holds at exponent \(a\). Then it holds at every exponent \(n=am\) with \(m\) odd.
depends_on: cor:all-regular-primary-local; lem:all-regular-compact-boundary; completed Kummer units; filling one cusp; Saidi2022 Propositions3.1/3.2 and TheoremB for the actual full cusp-section action

statement: [Scope of the bridge] \label{rem:allprime-bridge-scope} The proof uses all primes in geometric abelianization twice: to select the rational sign of a global affine unit, and to recover the full inertia parameter at a fixed cusp. It does not assert diagonality of the finite-abelian-descent adelic set of the proper curve at every regular exponent. It is a theorem for the specified finite-derived and prosolvable arithmetic quotients, with full local witnesses; it does not deduce such a theorem for an arbitrary geometric quotient or for a single-primary affine quotient.
depends_on: cor:all-regular-primary-local; lem:all-regular-compact-boundary; completed Kummer units; filling one cusp; Saidi2022 Propositions3.1/3.2 and TheoremB for the actual full cusp-section action

statement: \label{def:irreg-data} A \emph{compact \(p\)-Selmer datum on \(F_p\)} consists of \[ t\in H^1(\Q,T_pJ_p),\qquad R_v\in F_p(\Q_v)\quad(v<\infty), \] such that \begin{equation} \loc_v(t)=\kappa_{p,v}\bigl(j_p(R_v)\bigr) \quad\text{for every finite }v. \label{eq:irreg-data} \end{equation}
depends_on: McCallum2001 Propositions2/3 pp397-398 with complete proofs; Milne2006ADT finite duality/reciprocity; Masley1978 Theorem3.2 p310; Newman1970 Table2 p218; explicit wild quotient and fibre count

statement: \label{lem:irreg-reciprocity} Let \(A/\Q\) be principally polarized, and let \(u\in H^1(\Q,T_pA)\) have localizations \(\kappa_{p,v}(P_v)\), with \(P_v\in A(\Q_v)\) at every finite place. For every \(d\in H^1_{\{p\}}(\Q,A)[p^n]\), \begin{equation} \langle P_p,d_p\rangle_p=0 \label{eq:irreg-supported-pairing} \end{equation} under local Tate duality.
depends_on: McCallum2001 Propositions2/3 pp397-398 with complete proofs; Milne2006ADT finite duality/reciprocity; Masley1978 Theorem3.2 p310; Newman1970 Table2 p218; explicit wild quotient and fibre count

statement: \label{lem:irreg-tower-functional} Suppose a compatible tower \begin{equation} d=(d_n)_{n\geq1},\qquad d_n\in H^1_{\{p\}}(\Q,A)[p^n],\qquad p\,d_{n+1}=d_n, \label{eq:irreg-tower} \end{equation} has nonzero localization at \(p\). It determines a nonzero continuous homomorphism \begin{equation} \ell_d:A(\Q_p)\longrightarrow\Z_p. \label{eq:irreg-integral-functional} \end{equation} Its kernel contains all torsion and is saturated for multiplication by every nonzero integer. There is a nonzero invariant differential \(\omega_d\) on \(A/\Q_p\) such that \begin{equation} \ell_d(P)=\omega_d\bigl(\log_A(P)\bigr) \quad\text{for all }P\in A(\Q_p). \label{eq:irreg-log-functional} \end{equation} Every collection \(P_v\) occurring in Lemma~\ref{lem:irreg-reciprocity} satisfies \(\ell_d(P_p)=0\).
depends_on: McCallum2001 Propositions2/3 pp397-398 with complete proofs; Milne2006ADT finite duality/reciprocity; Masley1978 Theorem3.2 p310; Newman1970 Table2 p218; explicit wild quotient and fibre count

statement: \label{lem:irreg-quotient-free} The morphism \(f\) is the quotient by the free action \begin{equation} \mu_p\times F_p\longrightarrow F_p,\qquad \zeta\cdot(X:Y:Z)=(\zeta^bX:\zeta^{-a}Y:Z). \label{eq:irreg-action} \end{equation} In particular, \(f:F_p(\Q_p)\to C_{a,b,c}(\Q_p)\) is injective. Moreover \(j(O_0),j(O_1),j(O_\infty)\) are torsion points.

statement: \label{lem:irreg-wild-exists} For every prime \(p\geq5\), at least one of the quotients \(C_{1,k,-k-1}\), \(1\leq k\leq p-2\), is wild.

statement: [McCallum]\label{prop:irreg-McCallum} For \(C=C_{a,b,c}\) and \(A=\Jac(C)\) as above: \begin{enumerate} \item If \(r<(p+3)/8\), there is a compatible tower \[ d_n\in H^1_{\{p\}}(\Q,A)[p^n],\qquad p\,d_{n+1}=d_n, \] whose localization at \(p\) is nonzero. \item If \(C\) is wild, there is an affinoid \(\mathcal X\subset C(\C_p)\) containing \(C(\Q_p)\) such that, for every nonzero holomorphic differential \(\eta\) on \(C\), the Coleman integral \[ I_\eta(R)=\int_{O_0}^R\eta \] has at most \(p\) zeros in \(\mathcal X\). \end{enumerate}

statement: \label{thm:irreg-fixed} Suppose \begin{equation} r=\dim_{\F_p}\Cl(\Q(\zeta_p))/p\Cl(\Q(\zeta_p)) <\frac{p+3}{8}. \label{eq:irreg-Mc-bound} \end{equation} There is one finite set \(S_p\subset F_p(\Q_p)\), independent of the compact \(p\)-Selmer datum and of all its chosen local representatives, such that \begin{equation} \{Q_0,Q_1,Q_\infty\}\subseteq S_p,\qquad |S_p|\leq p, \label{eq:irreg-fixed-size} \end{equation} and every datum in Definition~\ref{def:irreg-data} has \(R_p\in S_p\). More precisely, one may choose any wild quotient \(C_{a,b,c}\); a single supported tower for its Jacobian, fixed independently of the datum, determines such a set.

statement: \label{rem:irreg-uniform} The set \(S_p\) need not be canonical: it depends on a fixed quotient and a fixed supported tower. Its defining choices are independent of the Selmer datum, which is the uniformity asserted in the theorem. Neither a first-case hypothesis nor finiteness of a Tate--Shafarevich group is used for the bound.

statement: \label{cor:irreg-fixed-discs} In addition to \eqref{eq:irreg-Mc-bound}, suppose either \eqref{eq:irreg-rank-bound} or the class-component hypothesis of Corollary~\ref{cor:irreg-cubic}. Then \(S_p\) may be replaced by its intersection with the three coordinate cusp residue discs while retaining all conclusions of Theorem~\ref{thm:irreg-fixed}.

statement: \label{cor:irreg-37-59-67} For \(p=37,59,67\), there is one fixed set \(S_p\subset F_p(\Q_p)\) containing the three rational cusps, contained in their three coordinate residue discs, and satisfying \[ 3\leq |S_p|\leq p, \] which contains the \(p\)-local centre of every compact \(p\)-Selmer datum on \(F_p\). For \(p=37\), one may use \(C_{37}:y^{37}=x(1-x)\), of genus \(18\), to construct \(S_{37}\). In particular, the same \(S_{37}\) works for every quotient section retaining the proper compact \(T_{37}J_{37}\) projection and having the stipulated full local representatives.

statement: \label{cor:irreg-higher-fixed} Let \(n=pm\) be odd and assume \eqref{eq:irreg-Mc-bound}. Put \(d=\gcd(m,p-1)\). There is one fixed finite set \(S_{n,p}\subset F_n(\Q_p)\) containing every \(\Q_p\)-rational coordinate boundary point, such that \begin{equation} |S_{n,p}|\leq(p-3)d^2+3d. \label{eq:irreg-higher-bound} \end{equation} It contains the \(p\)-local centre of every datum consisting of \[ t\in H^1(\Q,T_pJ_n),\qquad R_v\in F_n(\Q_v), \qquad \loc_v(t)=\kappa_{p,v}([R_v-Q_0]) \quad(v<\infty). \] If \(d=1\), the bound is \(p\). In particular \(d=1\) whenever \(p\) is the least prime divisor of \(n\).

statement: \label{prop:irreg-prescribed-isolation} If a wild quotient satisfies \eqref{eq:irreg-prescribed-tower}, then any compact \(p\)-Selmer datum on \(F_p\) whose \(p\)-local centre lies in a coordinate cusp residue disc has that cusp as its centre.

Let \(K_{\{p\}}(p)\) be the maximal pro-\(p\) extension of \(K\) unramified outside \(\mathfrak p\). Then the decomposition map \begin{equation} G_{K_{\mathfrak p}}\longrightarrow \Gal(K_{\{p\}}(p)/K) \label{eq:irreg-source-map} \end{equation} is not surjective.

Put \[ N_C=\pi_1(C_{\bar k})^{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}\ell}, \] and retain full \(G_k\) in the corresponding arithmetic quotient. statement: [The Frattini automorphism kernel] \label{lem:ff3-frattini} For a finitely generated pro-\(\ell\) group \(M\), \[ \ker\bigl(\operatorname{Aut}(M)\to \operatorname{Aut}(M/\Phi(M))\bigr) \] is pro-\(\ell\), where \(\Phi(M)=\overline{M^\ell[M,M]}\). statement: [A residual-trivial automorphism criterion] \label{lem:ff3-trivial-residual} Let \(C/k\) be a geometrically connected proper curve with \(b\in C(k)\) and finitely generated geometric pro-\(\ell\) group \(M\). statement: [The rational factors at thirty-seven] \label{prop:thirtyseven-factors} There is a rational isogeny $J\sim_{\mathbb Q}A\times P$, with $\dim A=6$, $\dim P=12$, and \[ \operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q}^0(J) =\mathbb Q\times\mathbb Q(\zeta_3),\qquad \operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q}^0(A)=\mathbb Q,\qquad \operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q}^0(P)=\mathbb Q(\zeta_3). \] Both factors are rationally simple, and \[ \operatorname{rank}A(\mathbb Q)\geq1,\qquad \operatorname{rank}P(\mathbb Q)\in2\mathbb Z_{\geq0},\qquad P(\mathbb Q)_{\mathrm{tors}}\simeq\mathbb Z/37\mathbb Z. \] Thus $P$ is the only possible positive-dimensional rational rank-zero isogeny factor of this $J$.
depends_on: GrossRohrlich1978 Theorem1.1 p202, Lemma1.6 pp206-207, Theorem2.1 pp208-209; ShuExpanded2021 Proposition3.12 p16/Theorem3.13 pp17-18; Zhang2001 TheoremA; Nekovar2012 equation0.3.1 and TheoremsA/B/B-prime; Hsieh2014 September2025 author Theorem2/Corollaries2-3; BurungaleHeTianYe2026 Theorem1.6/Corollary1.8

statement: [Conductor, signs, and the order-nine character] \label{prop:thirtyseven-character} The conductors and root numbers are \[ N(J)=37^{36},\quad N(A)=37^{12},\quad N(P)=37^{24}, \qquad W(J)=W(A)=-1,\quad W(P)=+1. \] Let $\chi$ be the character modulo $37$ with $\chi(2)=\zeta_9$. Over a coefficient field containing its values, \[ V(J)\simeq V(A)\oplus V(A)\otimes\chi \oplus V(A)\otimes\chi^2. \] The two complementary weight-two Hilbert constituents over the real sextic field $F_0$ have nontrivial cubic central characters.
depends_on: GrossRohrlich1978 Theorem1.1 p202, Lemma1.6 pp206-207, Theorem2.1 pp208-209; ShuExpanded2021 Proposition3.12 p16/Theorem3.13 pp17-18; Zhang2001 TheoremA; Nekovar2012 equation0.3.1 and TheoremsA/B/B-prime; Hsieh2014 September2025 author Theorem2/Corollaries2-3; BurungaleHeTianYe2026 Theorem1.6/Corollary1.8

statement: [Constant quintic point map through class three] \label{prop:ff3-quintic-depth-three} Let $q\ne3,5$ be a rational prime with $q\equiv1\pmod5$, let \[ C/\mathbb F_q:\ X^5+Y^5+Z^5=0,\qquad C_A:\ v^2+v=u^5,\qquad A=\operatorname{Jac}(C_A), \] and suppose arithmetic Frobenius on $A[3]$ has order twenty. Use $b=(0:-1:1)$ as base point and put \[ N=\pi_1(C_{\overline{\mathbb F}_q},b)^{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}3}. \] With closed ordinary lower-central terms, continuous nonabelian cohomology satisfies \[ H^1(G_{\mathbb F_q},N/\gamma_4N)=\{1\}. \] Thus every section of this arithmetic quotient is geometrically conjugate to the point section of $b$. In particular, the proper point-section map is constant in this quotient and in every finite Galois-stable quotient of $N$ of nilpotency class at most three. The set of rational primes satisfying these conditions has natural density $1/10$, and it contains $q=11$.
depends_on: Three quotient maps and integral norm identities; polarization; tensor-grade quotient; continuous full-procyclic cohomology; exact q11 point counts; conjugacy-stable Chebotarev set

statement: [A nontrivial diagonal twist cannot remove the residual obstruction] \label{prop:ff3-diagonal-twist-obstruction} Let $a\in\{5,7\}$, let $k=\mathbb F_Q$ have characteristic prime to $3a$, and assume $\mu_a\subset k$. On $C_a:X^a+Y^a+Z^a=0$, let \[ \delta(X:Y:Z)=(\zeta^rX:\zeta^sY:Z),\qquad r,s\in\mathbb Z/a\mathbb Z, \] where $\zeta$ is primitive. Let $N$ be the geometric pro-three fundamental group and let $F$ denote arithmetic Frobenius. If the action of $\delta^{-1}F$ on $N/\Phi(N)$ has three-power order, then $r=s=0$. In particular, for a nonidentity $\delta$, the closed subgroup of $\operatorname{Out}(N)$ generated by its twisted Frobenius cannot be pro-three.
depends_on: Three same-curve quotient maps; exact residual scalar fields; geometric surface characters and degree-two relation after DavisPriesWickelgren2024 author pp2-4; coprime Schur-Zassenhaus and compactness

statement: [The geometric diagonal centralizer has a nonzero quotient] \label{prop:ff3-diagonal-centralizer} Let $a\in\{5,7\}$ and let $C_a$ be the proper Fermat curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic prime to $3a$. Let $N$ be its geometric pro-three fundamental group and $H=(\mu_a)^2$ its diagonal automorphism group. Form the relative geometric action extension \[ 1\longrightarrow N\longrightarrow E_H\longrightarrow H \longrightarrow1, \] retaining the full finite quotient $H$. Choose any complement $S\subset E_H$, mapping isomorphically onto $H$, and let it act on $N$ by conjugation. Such a complement exists by coprime Schur--Zassenhaus. Put $L_2=\gamma_2N/\gamma_3N$ and $g=(a-1)(a-2)/2$. Then \[ Z_N(S)\subset\gamma_2N,\qquad \frac{Z_N(S)}{Z_N(S)\cap\gamma_3N} \simeq L_2^H\simeq\mathbb Z_3^{g-1}. \] In particular this quotient has rank five for $a=5$ and rank fourteen for $a=7$.
depends_on: Three same-curve quotient maps; exact residual scalar fields; geometric surface characters and degree-two relation after DavisPriesWickelgren2024 author pp2-4; coprime Schur-Zassenhaus and compactness

statement: [Fermat's theorem for Selmer sections]\label{thm:fermat} Let $n\geq3$ be odd. Every Selmer section of \eqref{eq:fundamental} is cuspidal. More precisely, if \[ y_1=(0:-1:1),\qquad y_2=(-1:0:1),\qquad y_3=(1:-1:0), \] then \begin{equation}\label{eq:packets} \Sec(U_n/\Q)^{\Sel}=\mathcal P_{y_1}\ \coprod\ \mathcal P_{y_2}\ \coprod\ \mathcal P_{y_3}. \end{equation} Each packet is naturally a torsor under \[ H^1(\Q,\Zhat(1))\simeq\varprojlim_m\Q^\times/(\Q^\times)^m. \] The inputs are the refined form of Serre's modularity theorem, Stoll's Theorem~8.2 and Corollary~8.8 with his 2017 corrections, Mazur's torsion theorem, and Stix's cusp-packet theorem. No local section conjecture is an input to this assertion.
depends_on: eq:fundamental

statement: [All sections, with its local input]\label{cor:all} Assume Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:local}. For every odd $n\geq3$, every section of \eqref{eq:fundamental} is Selmer and therefore cuspidal. Its entire section set is the disjoint union \eqref{eq:packets}. The only further local input is the established real section theorem.
depends_on: eq:fundamental; eq:packets; hyp:local

statement: [Two consequences of finite descent and the real place] \label{thm:other} If the smooth modular curve $X_1(N)/\Q$ has positive genus, every Selmer section of $Y_1(N)/\Q$ is cuspidal at a rational cusp. Under Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:local}, the same assertion holds for every full section. For every even integer $n\geq2$, $U_n/\Q$ has no Selmer section and, in fact, no full section. The latter assertion needs only the real section theorem, not Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:local}.
depends_on: hyp:local

statement: Even plus exponents n>=2 admit no full profinite section, hence no Selmer section.

[Finite support]\label{lem:finite-support} Let $U/k$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine curve whose smooth proper compactification $X$ has genus at least one. Let $s$ be Selmer. Suppose there is a finite reduced subscheme $Z\subset X$ such that its local centers belong to $Z(k_v)$ at a density-one set of finite places. Then $s$ is the section of a point of $U(k)$, or is cuspidal at a point of $(X\setminus U)(k)$.

[Cuspidal Legendre class]\label{prop:cusp-class} At every geometric cusp of $F_n$, over any characteristic-zero field over which that cusp is rational, a parameter $t$ can be chosen so that \begin{equation}\label{eq:jinverse} j^{-1}=2^{-8}t^{2n} \frac{(1+t^n)^2}{(1+t^n+t^{2n})^3}. \end{equation} The Tate parameter satisfies $q=j^{-1}+O(j^{-2})$. Hence every cusp section satisfies \[ \kappa(q)(s)=\kappa(2^{-8})+2n\,\kappa(t)(s). \] In particular, for $n=\ell$ prime, \begin{equation}\label{eq:cuspresidual} [q(s)]_\ell=[2^{-8}]_\ell\in H^1(k,\mu_\ell). \end{equation} The residual Legendre representation is a quadratic twist of the Tate extension with this class; the extension need not split.
[Reducibility]\label{prop:reducible} For every Selmer section $s$ of $U_\ell$, $\ell\geq5$ prime, $\overline\rho_s$ is reducible over $\F_\ell$.

\label{prop:fourlevel} For a Selmer section of $U_\ell$, $\ell\geq5$ prime, there is a geometrically connected finite \et ale section neighborhood $V\to U_\ell$ whose smooth proper compactification admits a nonconstant morphism to $X_0(4\ell)$.
[The cubic]\label{prop:cubic} Every Selmer section of $U_3/\Q$ is cuspidal, and $F_3(\Q)=\{y_1,y_2,y_3\}$.

[Affine consequence of the proper local theorem] \label{prop:local-affine} Assume Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:local} over a fixed finite extension $k/\Q_p$. Every full section of a smooth affine hyperbolic curve $U/k$ is a point section or a section at a $k$-rational cusp.
depends_on: hyp:local

statement: \label{def:selmer} A section of a smooth affine hyperbolic curve $U/k$, with smooth proper compactification $X$, is \emph{Selmer} if at every finite place $v$ its restriction is the section of a point of $U(k_v)$ or a section in a decomposition group of a point of $(X\setminus U)(k_v)$. At a real place we require a real point section or a real cusp section. There is no additional condition at complex places. This definition uses the full profinite groups.
depends_on: Point and decomposition-group sections; full profinite convention

statement: [Proper local section input]\label{hyp:local} For every prime $p$, every finite extension $k/\Q_p$, and every smooth proper geometrically connected curve $X/k$ of genus at least two, the point map \[ X(k)\longrightarrow\Sec(X/k) \] is bijective for the full profinite arithmetic fundamental group.
depends_on: OpenAI2026 October6 Theorem1.1 p2; unrefereed

statement: [Lifting local geometry]\label{lem:lifting} Let $U/k$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine curve, and let $s$ be a Selmer section. A connected finite \et ale cover $V\to U$ to which $s$ lifts is geometrically connected, and the lifted section is Selmer. If $X_V$ is its smooth proper compactification, the local point-or-cusp centers give a point of $X_V(\A_k)_\bullet^{\fcov}$.

[A map to a curve controlled by descent]\label{cor:descent-map} In the setting of Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-support}, suppose there is a nonconstant morphism $f:X\to W$ to a smooth proper curve such that \[ W(\A_k)_\bullet^{\fab}=W(k). \] Then every Selmer section of $U$ is a point section or a cusp section.
depends_on: lem:finite-support

statement: [The constant in a formal Kummer class]\label{lem:kummer} Let $k$ have characteristic zero, let $t$ be a parameter at a rational boundary point, and suppose $q=a t^e h(t)$ with $a\in k^\times$, $e\in\Z$, and $h(t)\in1+t k[[t]]$. For any section $s$ of the punctured local fundamental group, \begin{equation}\label{eq:kummer} \kappa(q)(s)=\kappa(a)+e\,\kappa(t)(s) \quad\text{in }H^1(k,\Zhat(1)). \end{equation} Here $\kappa$ denotes the multiplicative Kummer map, written additively.

[The cusp above infinity]\label{rem:infinity} The quadratic twist at infinity is not independent of the section. For the Legendre equation, $c_6=32(\lambda+1)(\lambda-2)(2\lambda-1)$, and with $\lambda=-t^{-\ell}$ one has \[ -c_4/c_6=\tfrac14t^\ell(1+O(t^\ell)). \] Its square class is ramified in the parameter for odd $\ell$. The local monodromy is $-T^{2\ell}$ rather than $T^{2\ell}$, where $T$ is a unipotent transvection. Pulling back the quadratic character along a cusp section can therefore depend on its tangent Kummer class. The global patching below permits arbitrary local quadratic inertia characters and includes precisely this possibility.

[Local ordinary points]\label{lem:local-points} Let $(a,b)\in U_\ell(\Q_p)$, so $a^\ell+b^\ell+1=0$, and set $\lambda=-a^\ell$. At an odd prime $p$, the Legendre curve has good reduction or is, after a quadratic twist, a Tate curve with $\ell\mid v_p(q)$. At $p=2$ it is potentially multiplicative and \[ v_2(q)\equiv-8\pmod\ell. \]

[Local residual conditions]\label{lem:local-residual} At every finite prime $p$ there is a quadratic character $\eps_p$ such that $\overline\rho_s\otimes\eps_p$ has the following properties: it is unramified if $p\neq2,\ell$; it is finite flat at $p=\ell$; and at $p=2$ it is tamely ramified with conductor exponent one.
\label{lem:modulargenus} For an odd prime $\ell$, \[ g(X_0(4\ell))=\frac{\ell-3}{2}. \]
[The rational torsion contradiction]\label{lem:torsion} For every prime $\ell\geq5$, $U_\ell(\Q)=\varnothing$.

[High-genus neighborhoods]\label{lem:highgenus} Let $U/k$ be a smooth affine hyperbolic curve in characteristic zero and let $s$ be a full section. The section neighborhoods whose smooth proper compactifications have genus at least two are cofinal.
